8546e04602f8e993: BANDAR PERMAISURI, Sept 19 — A man was killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) he was driving collided with a trailer lorry at Kilometre 38 of Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kota Bharu near Sungai Tong here last night.

Setiu district police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the accident at 12.01am and identified the victim as Mohd Assfarizal Salim, 44, of Taman Balok Pelangi, Kuantan, Pahang.

“Initial investigations found that the accident is believed to have occurred at about 11.30pm when the Perodua Alza MPV lost control and entered the opposite lane before colliding with a Volvo trailer lorry.

“The MPV driver was trapped inside the vehicle and was extricated by firefighters before being taken to Setiu Hospital for treatment after sustaining serious injuries. He later died at about 4.10am today,” he said in a statement today.
Zahril Asri said the lorry driver, who was travelling from Jertih to Kuantan, was uninjured, adding that police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

He urged anyone who witnessed the incident to come forward to the Setiu district police headquarters traffic division or contact investigating officer Inspector Aliah Syafinah Ani Sarudin at 013-6706156 to assist with the investigation. — Bernama
812285a5b7d4746d: NEW YORK: Protesters and police were expected to greet concertgoers in Philadelphia on Saturday for pop superstar Ed Sheeran's first show since he became embroiled in controversy set off by his opening act's pro-Palestinian comments.

Rapper Macklemore was booted from Sheeran's US Loop Tour on Monday after the owners of stadiums hosting upcoming shows objected to his shouting "Free Palestine" onstage in New Jersey earlier this month.
Sheeran has denied being behind the decision to remove Macklemore, saying his tour's promoter was responsible.

But four supporting acts soon quit the "Shape of You" singer's tour. They included Sheeran's backing band as well as performer Finneas, who rose to fame collaborating with his pop superstar sister Billie Eilish.
At a time when a growing number of artists are speaking out against the conflict in Gaza and West Bank settler violence, the 35-year-old British performer has maintained his apolitical stance.

"I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn't mean I don't have them, and it doesn't mean I don't care," he said on Instagram on Tuesday.
However, he said, "those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum."
The former busker-turned-superstar, accused by critics of failing to stand up to the stadium owners, has been targeted by boycott calls over the controversy.

"Clearly, there's some real discontent around how this whole situation is being managed, and he's definitely having to do some brand reputation management," said Gretchen Larsen, a professor specializing in the music industry at Durham University Business School in the UK.

No new opening acts or backing bands have been announced, and it was not known how Sheeran planned to carry out his show at Lincoln Financial Field in the eastern US city of Philadelphia on Saturday night.
A pro-Palestinian rally organised by local groups was scheduled to take place near the venue in the afternoon.
City police told AFP there would be an "appropriate police presence" to "help ensure the safety of concertgoers, employees and neighbourhood residents."
On the resale market, tickets for the show have been changing hands at a slightly brisker pace since Monday when compared to previous dates on Sheeran's tour, according to tracking site TicketData.

"Some share of the audience isn't tuned in to anything political, or is completely indifferent to it, and has only just now become aware that Ed Sheeran is even playing their city. They're buying tickets with zero connection to the controversy," site founder Keith Pagello said.
The price of the cheapest tickets had fallen from US$123 on Monday to US$67 by Friday afternoon.
Pagello said the decline was not necessarily linked to the row, as it is common for concert ticket prices to drop as the event date approaches.--AFP
18ea020f05a1b0ae: NAGOYA: Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani said on Saturday that politicians should not be involved in sports, following a diplomatic incident involving a Taiwan government official at the Asian Games.

Taiwan sport minister Lee Yang, a former Olympic badminton champion, was initially blocked from attending a flag-raising ceremony at the Games on Friday, triggering a standoff as the Taiwan delegation refused to participate in protest.
Lee Yang was eventually permitted entry, with the ceremony taking place more than an hour after scheduled.
Taiwan's cabinet complained Lee Yang had been subject to "unreasonable obstruction" in a statement and that he had obtained the required access credentials.
Sheikh Joaan said at a press conference he was unaware of the incident but that politicians needed to stay out of sports at the quadrennial Games.

"I think that our focus here is on the athletes and on making sure that everyone, all the athletes, have the equal rights in competing and in having their freedom," the Qatari told reporters in Nagoya.
"So I don't think the politicians or politics should be involved in sports. That's my opinion."
OCA Director General Husain Al-Musallam added that the flag-raising ceremony was meant for the participants in the Games.
"(It's) not for the delegation from the ministry or from the government," he said.
Lee Yang claimed back-to-back badminton gold medals in the men's doubles at the Tokyo and Paris Olympics.
The buildup to the Aichi-Nagoya Games has been overshadowed by complaints from national team delegations over organisational issues, including transport and the accommodations provided for athletes.
Sheikh Joaan defended the local organisers saying they had been solving accommodation issues as they arise.
"I think everything is hopefully being back on track," he said.
The organisational problems have underscored the massive size of the Games, which include a record 43 sports and 469 medal events, dwarfing the summer Olympics' 32 sports and 329 events.
The OCA defended the size of the programme at Nagoya, which will see the debut of "virtual" taekwondo while retaining breaking (breakdancing) and esports.
"We are very proud that the Asian Games (are) bigger than any other games with low cost," said Al-Musallam. - Reuters
9cf3eccafd99d26b: KUALA LUMPUR: A cloud seeding operation will be conducted today and tomorrow to reduce the impact of haze in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Selangor.

The operation will be conducted by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).

Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the cloud seeding operation was being conducted following PM2.5 readings in the affected areas exceeding 150 for more than 24 hours, based on readings issued by the Department of Environment (DoE).
"The operation will involve the relevant agencies, with an RMAF C-130 Hercules aircraft serving as the main asset for the cloud seeding operation.
"However, the operation is subject to weather conditions and the presence of suitable clouds for the cloud seeding process," he said.
He added that the operation was among the government's efforts to help reduce the impact of haze and improve air quality in the affected areas.

According to the DoE's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), air quality monitoring stations in Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur and Selangor were among 17 stations that recorded unhealthy API readings as of 1pm today.
Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 111, while Cheras and Batu Muda recorded readings of 139 and 124 respectively. Shah Alam in Selangor recorded an API reading of 154.

Seven of the air quality monitoring stations that recorded unhealthy API readings were in Sarawak. Serian recorded the highest reading at 176, followed by Kuching at 172, Sri Aman at 166, Samarahan at 165, Sibu at 158, Sarikei at 150 and Bintulu at 103.
d6a8840a3956b77d: NAGOYA: India have replaced their male flagbearer in Saturday's Asian Games opening ceremony in Nagoya, Japan, because the original choice, Tajinderpal Singh Toor, has not received his official ceremonial kit and cannot attend the event, media reports said.
Tajinderpal, who is aiming for his third straight Asian Games gold in shot put, will be replaced by kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat as the male flagbearer.
Shooter Manu Bhaker, who won two bronze medals at the Paris Olympics, is the female flagbearer.

"I'm told that my kit will reach at 3pm. at the airport. Reaching the opening ceremony venue after collecting my kit from airport on time will be very difficult. So, I've told IOA (Indian Olympic Association) that I'm not coming for opening ceremony," news agency PTI quoted Tajinderpal as saying.
"My kit is lying in India ... IOA told me yesterday about me becoming flagbearer. Otherwise my coach, who reached here yesterday, could've picked it up for me."
The IOA said in a statement that 31-year-old Tajinderpal would not be able to be India's flagbearer "due to a technical issue." - Reuters
0a5efca626839f70: SINGAPORE, Sept 19 — A healthcare company’s chief financial officer nearly transferred S$120,000 (RM384,000) to scammers after they impersonated the firm’s chairman and managing director on Microsoft Teams.

The attempted fraud came amid a sharp rise in business e-mail compromise scams in Singapore, with losses reaching S$57.3 million (RM183.4 million) in the first half of 2026, up from S$19.5 million (RM62.4 million) a year earlier.

“Everything happened so quickly. The scammers acted with a sense of urgency that made my colleague anxious to get the job done,” Jane (not her real name), one of the company’s directors, was quoted as saying by The Straits Times in a report published today.
“The instruction was just to ‘do it now’,” the 72-year-old added, stressing that the urgency made it difficult for her colleague to stop and question the instructions.

According to the newspaper’s report, the incident began when the company’s chief financial officer was asked by people posing as the chairman and managing director to submit the firm’s financial statements through a Teams group chat.

The scammers then instructed her to transfer S$120,000 from the company’s bank account, but she only realised she had been tricked after speaking to the real managing director, who denied giving the instruction.
The fraudsters sounded legitimate and communicated well in English, making the request appear more convincing.
“When instructions appear to come from the two most prominent figures in the company, how do you reject that request?” Jane asked.
The company’s payment protocol ultimately prevented the loss, as payment slips had to be physically signed before any bank transfer could be authorised.
“If not for that, the S$120,000 would have been lost. And the scammers’ next request may be for a larger amount,” she said.
The company then instructed UOB to monitor large transactions and ensure transfers were made only after proper authorisation.
UOB branch manager Carlene Lam said she contacted the bank’s Risk and Anti-Fraud teams after Jane reported the incident to assess what had happened and put safeguards in place.

“I assured Jane that safeguards were in place and contacted my colleagues in the Risk and Anti-Fraud teams to assess the incident and take the necessary precautions to protect Jane’s organisation, including verifying all payment instructions,” she was quoted as saying.

UOB head of group compliance Daniel Ng said such scams had evolved beyond conventional e-mails, with criminals increasingly using messaging, voice and video platforms to impersonate trusted executives.

“Scammers increasingly exploit messaging, voice and video channels – including AI-enabled impersonation – to pose as trusted executives and trick employees into making fraudulent fund transfers,” he told The Straits Times.

“As these scams become more sophisticated, businesses should treat unexpected or urgent payment instructions with caution and independently verify them through established channels before acting,” he added.
Singapore police recorded 262 business e-mail compromise cases in the first six months of 2026, up from 156 in the same period last year, making it the third-largest scam category by amount lost.
The scams typically involve criminals impersonating suppliers, vendors, clients or senior executives to trick employees into transferring company funds to fraudulent bank accounts.

Adrian Hia, managing director for Asia Pacific at cybersecurity firm Kaspersky, said the scams were particularly effective because they exploited familiar communication channels and workplace hierarchies.
He said employees could be less likely to question requests from senior executives, particularly when they were framed as urgent.

“Essentially, the authority associated with a high-ranking executive can work to reduce a recipient’s level of scrutiny and encourage immediate action rather than verification. Business e-mail compromise attacks succeed not only because of technical deception, but because they leverage authority and social workplace expectations,” he was quoted as saying.
Hia said warning signs included unexpected payment requests, particularly those outside established procedures.
Requests to transfer money to new or unfamiliar bank accounts, or where payment details differ from previous transactions, should also be independently verified.

Other red flags include instructions to bypass standard approval procedures or keep the request confidential, as well as unusual sign-in links, unsolicited attachments and unexpected login prompts when opening files.
76a30d3114a2323b: WASHINGTON: Google's consumer AI model Gemini hacked multiple systems through guessing login credentials, the company told AFP on Friday, the latest case of rogue AI cybersecurity transgressions, which have generated safety concerns.
The hacks, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, took place in May and were discovered by Google in July.

"In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test," Heather Adkins, Google's vice president of security engineering, told AFP in a statement.
"In all three of these instances, the model stopped," Adkins added, without specifying which organisations were breached.
"We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they've now made to their testing processes."
In July, two OpenAI models escaped the closed environment they were meant to stay in, got onto the internet on their own and broke into the internal systems AI platform Hugging Face.
The incident fed worries that AI giants cannot keep their own models under control, as similar episodes have been reported at Anthropic and China's Moonshot AI.
"These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly," Adkins emphasised.--AFP
aee74698089870db: MASJID TANAH: Fishermen in Kampung Pasir Gembur, Tanjung Bidara, will receive a new RM270,000 fishing hall next month, courtesy of Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
The initiative aims to ensure the safety and welfare of fishermen when setting out to sea and returning home with their catch.
Pasir Gembur Fishermen Association chairman Rusli Othman said the commitment ends a decade-long wait for a modern facility.
He said the new hall will streamline daily operations for 27 local fishermen, from preparing their gear to landing their daily catch.

"Alhamdulillah, to me this is a major success for Datuk Seri Ab Rauf himself. He has proven that he does not just make empty promises, but is committed to delivering what was pledged to our fishing community.
"Moving forward, launching and hauling boats ashore will be much safer without needing to build momentum like a jet ski. Equipment and boat storage will also be far more organised," he said.
Earlier, Rauf, accompanied by Rural Development, Agriculture and Food Security Committee chairman Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, officiated the groundbreaking ceremony for the facility.
During the event, fishermen were also presented with GPS Finder devices to assist in navigation and locating fish stocks.
Rusli said the local fishing community was delighted to receive the devices, noting that such equipment is usually costly but highly sought after for pinpointing large schools of fish.
He expressed gratitude for the Chief Minister's initiative, adding that the technology will make trips safer and boost catches.
Meanwhile, 60-year-old fisherman Mustaffa Che Man said the new hall brings renewed hope to local fishermen, giving them proper comfort for their daily operations.
Another fisherman, Mohd Fazli Baba, 43, said the GPS devices will help prevent fishermen from getting lost at sea during bad weather or low visibility.
"I once got lost and drifted as far as Pantai Puteri and Pulau Besar because I did not have a GPS device to guide me back.
"Having this device will make it much easier to track fish and navigate back to our hall safely," he said.
In September last year, Rauf visited the site to inspect the previous 40-year-old facility, which had fallen into disrepair.
Following the visit, he convened a meeting with fishermen representatives and relevant government agencies to expedite the construction of the new fishing hall.
d4d23f994b1c5dff: MASJID TANAH: The Melaka government has disbursed RM7.53 million in welfare assistance to benefit 5,775 recipients across the state.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said that as of July, RM4.45 million was distributed to 2,439 recipients under the Bantuan Melaka Sayang Rakyat (MeSRa) Am Kebajikan programme.
He added that over RM3.08 million was allocated under the MeSRa disposable diapers and MeSRa milk for bedridden patients programmes, benefiting 3,345 recipients across Melaka's three districts.
"Efforts to expand the welfare network reflect the state government's commitment to ensuring that those in need are not left behind in the state's development," he said.

"All this sends a clear message that the welfare of the people will remain an important part of Melaka's development agenda, as we want the state's progress to move forward with compassion, inclusiveness, and a spirit of togetherness down to the grassroots."

Rauf, who is also Tanjung Bidara assemblyman, said this when officiating the state-level Senior Citizens, Persons with Disabilities, and Children's Day celebration in conjunction with the Tanjung Bidara constituency Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR) programmeat Villa D'Aqua, Kampung Pulau, here.

Present were State Secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh, Women, Family and Community Development Committee chairman Datuk Kalsom Noordin, and Tourism, Heritage, Arts and Culture Committee chairman Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman.
Rauf said these initiatives stem from the MeSRa concept, which forms the foundation of the state administration as a responsibility to be translated into action rather than just a slogan.
"The state government will continue to ensure welfare aspects are given attention alongside efforts to develop the economy and improve the people's well-being," he said.
During the event, Rauf visited Muhammad Aish Irfan Mohammad Hakeem, a child with disabilities, in Taman Bidara Palma.
He presented the child's family with a Tabung Bantuan Segera contribution, a PwD card, and a Ziarah Kasih kit as a gesture of care and support.

Rauf also launched the new Seri Kemunting Community-Based Rehabilitation Centre (PDK) office in the same residential area, presenting the Insentif Belanja Rakyat and PDK Trainee Rehabilitation Aid Incentives.
6d0100554afbcfc0: KUALA LUMPUR: A heavy defeat to South Korea has given the Malaysian women's basketball team a clear focus for their remaining Group C matches at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
Malaysia were beaten 106-40 by the World Cup-level side at the Aichi International Arena on Friday.
Guard Chong Yin Yin said the defeat was a valuable learning experience.
"We were against a World Cup-level team. They just finished their World Cup and had a good performance. My coach told us to go for the challenge and learn from them," said the 33-year-old.
She said the coaching staff wanted the players to study Korea's tactics rather than focus on the scoreline.
"Our coach's message was to pay attention to how they were playing, what was their strategy, their defence. And we tried to catch up," she said.
Despite the heavy defeat, Yin Yin provided a bright spot for Malaysia by sinking two three-pointers.
She credited a teammate's pass for the opportunity and said the baskets lifted the team's energy.
"My teammate made a very good pass to me. I made the three, and I felt my whole team got a boost of energy," she said.
Malaysia next face Taiwan on Sunday before completing their Group C campaign against Mongolia on Tuesday.
Yin Yin said the team must improve defensively in their upcoming fixtures.
"We need better defence. We will play against Taiwan, who are a strong team. We will fight as we can. And Mongolia we try again, we will go for the win," she said.
464b3022bffc1f64: KAJANG, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has recorded statements from Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu and the ministry’s secretary-general in connection with an investigation into the delays in the supply of fertiliser in Kedah.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Mohamad’s statement was recorded on September 16, while the secretary-general’s statement was recorded a day earlier.

He added that, so far, 37 witnesses had been called and their statements recorded to assist in the investigation, which began on August 26, regarding the appointment of a company by the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM).
“The investigation is still ongoing, and is expected to be finalised within another week or two,” he told a press conference here today.

Abd Halim said the MACC would also record statements from several more witnesses to complete the investigation, which is being conducted under Section 471 of the Penal Code concerning the offence of using documents known or believed to be forged.
He said that, at this stage, MACC believes there are criminal elements and governance-related issues in the case, but is more focused on the criminal aspects.
“We will set aside the governance issues for now because we are focusing on the criminal aspects. However, I cannot comment further because the investigation is still ongoing,” he added.

Previously, MACC’s initial investigation found that a company was supposed to supply 616,015 bags of fertiliser, but until September only 333,655 bags had been supplied, leaving a shortfall of 282,360 bags.

The investigation papers were opened following a complaint regarding allegations that the fertiliser supplier appointed by KPKM failed to supply fertiliser under the Paddy Production Incentive Scheme (SIPP) in areas under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada). — Bernama
29abc4f995437223: PUTRAJAYA: The government will continue to strengthen pondok schools through infrastructure upgrades and the introduction of new fields of knowledge, including artificial intelligence (AI).
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was crucial to ensuring pondok schools remained relevant while staying true to the Islamic scholarly tradition at their core.
He said aid could be provided to selected pondok schools to serve as models.
"It cannot just be about physical facilities, but also about the disciplines of knowledge," he said at the National Turath Ulama Muzakarah 2026.
Anwar said various administrations had governed the country since independence, but he wanted efforts to strengthen pondok schools to be pursued with greater resolve.
He said government assistance should be seen as an effort to uplift pondok schools, including by providing better facilities for students.
"First, the pondok itself must be elevated. This is the government's role: to assist and refine it. Pondok schools must also accept new curricula," he said.
At the same time, Anwar said introducing new subjects did not mean abandoning traditional texts and Islamic scholarship, but adapting to current needs.
He cited AI as a key discipline to prioritise, noting its vast potential for dakwah and the advancement of Islam.
However, he warned that using AI without ethical and moral frameworks could pose serious risks to Muslims.
"AI is an important tool in dakwah and the spread of Islam, but AI without ethics and morality can become a major problem and an enemy that will wound us," he said.
Anwar said pondok students must be exposed to and trained in the technology so they do not remain mere end-users, but fully understand its benefits and risks.
"Therefore, we must train the youths in pondok to master it," he said.

Present at the event were Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, former Grand Mufti of Egypt Sheikh Ali Jum'ah and prominent scholar Sheikh Prof Dr Sayyid Idris al-Fasi.
8b8a3a84a1ab2407: KAJANG, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission (MACC) has issued notices to former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim and his family members requiring them to declare their assets within a month.
According to Berita Harian (BH), MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the notices were handed to Azeez and his children this week under legal provisions.

“We have already served notices on Datuk Seri Azeez and his family to declare their assets within a month as provided under the law. The notices were delivered together with the relevant forms for reporting to MACC,” he told BH at a press conference after officiating an event at Kajang Prison College today.
On September 9, Azeez was charged with one count under Section 23 of the MACC Act.
As of September 18, MACC has charged six individuals in connection with eight cases under the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), while five other investigations remain ongoing.
868474372e2c0266: SINGAPORE, Sept 19 — Singapore Airlines (SIA) has reclaimed the title of the world’s best airline, while Malaysia’s AirAsia retained its crown as the world’s best low-cost carrier in the latest Skytrax rankings.

SIA displaced Qatar Airways, which topped the 2025 rankings, while Hong Kong’s Cathay Pacific Airways, Japan’s ANA All Nippon Airways and Turkish Airlines rounded out the top five, The Straits Times reported today.
The win is SIA’s sixth in the history of the World Airline Awards, with its previous victory coming in 2023.
The Singapore carrier finished second behind Qatar Airways in 2025.

For Malaysian travellers, AirAsia’s showing provides a regional talking point, with the carrier named the world’s best low-cost airline for a record 17th consecutive year, while SIA’s low-cost subsidiary Scoot retained the world’s best long-haul low-cost airline title for a sixth straight year.
The rankings are based on a Skytrax survey conducted from September 2025 to August 2026, involving more than 24.8 million travellers from more than 100 nationalities who rated more than 300 airlines.
AirAsia was named world’s best low-cost airline by Skytrax for a record 17th consecutive year in 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif

SIA also won the awards for best airline in Asia, world’s best economy class and world’s best economy class onboard catering, while finishing second behind Cathay Pacific for the world’s best cabin crew.
SIA chief executive officer Goh Choon Phong said the award reflected the dedication and professionalism of the airline’s staff and thanked customers for their continued trust and support.

“We are grateful to our customers for their trust and support, and we are committed to delivering an exceptional, world-class travel experience every time they fly with us,” he was quoted as saying by the Singapore newspaper.

SIA Group recorded its highest-ever revenue of S$20.5 billion (RM64.6 billion) in the 2025/26 financial year, while SIA and Scoot carried a record 42.2 million passengers between April 2025 and March 2026.
The carrier is also preparing to introduce new first- and business-class seats on its Airbus A350-900 fleet, although the rollout has been delayed to the first quarter of 2027.
The new seats were initially scheduled to debut in the second quarter of 2026 and were also intended for Boeing’s 777-9 aircraft, whose production has faced delays.
6db7a2cb24418ba1: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should explain the legal framework, procedures and criteria that will be used to implement house arrest involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali also wants the government to explain whether the same privilege could be considered for other prisoners who meet the required criteria.

To ensure transparency in the implementation of the Pardons Board's decision, he said Bersatu also demanded that all conditions imposed on Najib, including serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, be clearly detailed and announced to the public.
"This is important to avoid the perception that there is one form of treatment for the nobility and influential individuals, and another for ordinary citizens.
"This explanation will prevent public unease that could undermine the integrity of the judiciary and public confidence in the legal and integrity systems," he said in a statement today.

It was reported yesterday that Najib was granted house arrest for the remainder of his sentence on condition that he pays the RM50 million fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.

The Federal Territories Pardons Board, in a statement, had said that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
485e0a5a0c19e9fa: PETALING JAYA: The lawyer representing Tengku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar has urged the Negeri Sembilan executive council to push for disciplinary action to be taken against state secretary Zafir Ibrahim for refusing to gazette a proclamation on the state ruler's purported removal.

Emirul Sarifudin Nor Azmi, who is also representing the four purported undangs and Tunku Besar Tampin, accused Zafir of committing misconduct by refusing to gazette the proclamation as ordered by the Negeri Sembilan executive council.
Emirul claimed the state secretary was overstepping his bounds and barring the purported new ruler, Tengku Nadzaruddin, from executing his constitutional powers.

"Based on these offences, I urge the exco to ask the chief secretary to the government to commence disciplinary proceedings against Zafir and to transfer him from his position as state secretary," he said in a statement.
On Thursday, menteri besar Ismail Lasim endorsed a statement issued by his exco that purportedly affirmed Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir’s removal as Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
He said the state secretary had been asked to proceed with gazetting the proclamation “according to the relevant regulations”.

However, the state secretary’s office said it will not proceed with gazetting the proclamation, given the Attorney-General’s Chambers’ (AGC) view that the proclamation dated April 19 was invalid and unconstitutional.
Emirul, however, argued that the views of the AGC were merely an opinion, not a binding order.
"What's binding on the state secretary is the exco's executive decision," he said.

306a451abf742d66: PETALING JAYA: An MIC leader has urged the education ministry to explain reports that tuition centres will be required to possess 30% Bumiputera equity by 2027 or their licences will not be renewed.

While respecting efforts to boost Bumiputera participation in the economy, MIC strategic director C Sivaraj said this cannot be done by forcibly taking the rights and equity of non-Bumiputera communities.

"If someone started their business years ago with their own capital and has built their reputation, provided jobs and complied with all regulations, why should they now be forced to relinquish part of their equity simply to renew their licence?
"The government's policymaking authority must be used carefully, especially when it involves businesses that have operated legitimately for a long time.

"We cannot strengthen one race at the expense of another," he said in a statement, adding that this move would affect many Indian operators of tuition centres who have built their businesses over many years.
Sivaraj urged the education ministry to clarify whether this 30% equity rule would apply to all existing tuition centres, and whether there would be a grace period for operators.

Earlier this week, Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung said a ministry guideline purportedly stated that tuition centres must have 30% Bumiputera equity in order to have their licences renewed next year.
Lee urged the ministry to explain the basis for the move and to consult operators and give them clear guidance on the implementation of the policy.
32eccab3bedc87d5: KOTA BARU: Three Rohingya workers, including a woman, and a local employer have been remanded for seven days over the death of a fellow Rohingya outside a Muslim cemetery in Taman Desa Kujid here last night.

The remand order, which begins tomorrow, was issued by Magistrate Tuan Fakhrul Razzi Abd Hamid at the Magistrates' Court here today. The suspects, aged between 25 and 40, are being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
All four suspects arrived at the court at 9.30am.
Police detained four people, including a woman, following the death of an 18-year-old Rohingya man at a kongsi house opposite the Taman Desa Kujid Muslim cemetery here last night.
Police were informed of the incident at 10.30pm, and initial investigations found that the victim died at the scene after suffering a neck injury believed to have been caused by a sharp object.
Two suspects, the employer and a Rohingya man, were detained at the scene, while the woman and another Rohingya man were arrested in Selising, Pasir Puteh, near here.
1895cfa3fe0c2a47: KAJANG: Status kes 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) dihadapi Najib Razak kekal tidak berubah walaupun bekas perdana menteri itu diberikan pengampunan bersyarat, kata Ketua Pesuruhjaya Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM), Abd Halim Aman.

“Bagi pihak kami, kes-kes yang masih tertangguh akan kekal seperti biasa. Seperti yang ada sekarang, status quo kekal,” katanya pada sidang media di sini hari ini.
Beliau berkata demikian ketika ditanya sama ada pengampunan bersyarat diberikan kepada Najib akan memberikan kesan terhadap kes 1MDB dan rayuan yang masih berjalan.
Halim berkata, sesuatu kes tidak boleh disamakan dengan kes yang lain kerana setiap siasatan melibatkan tuduhan dan isu berlainan.

“Kita perlu faham bahawa setiap kes adalah berbeza antara satu sama lain. Ia tidak boleh dikendalikan sebagai kes yang sama dan kes-kes itu berbeza memandangkan sesuatu siasatan itu ditujukan kepada apa yang sedang disiasat, berhubung isu tertentu yang dibangkitkan atau aduan yang dibuat,” katanya.

Semalam, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim memperkenankan pengampunan bersyarat kepada Najib untuk menjalani baki hukuman secara tahanan di rumah hingga 23 Ogos 2028, tertakluk sekiranya beliau membayar denda RM50 juta.

d6d4e769400bfe99: IPOH, Sept 19 — Three motorcyclists were killed and nine others injured in a crash involving 12 motorcycles and three cars along Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here early today.
Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the incident was reported at 3.35am, Harian Metro (HM) reported.
Preliminary investigations showed all 15 vehicles were heading from Meru towards Tambun when the collision occurred.

“Two motorcyclists aged 19 and 20 were confirmed dead at the scene. Nine others, aged between 19 and 25, who sustained injuries were taken to Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital (HRPB) for treatment,” he said in a statement to HM.
Another 19 year old rider died while receiving treatment in HRPB’s Emergency and Trauma Department, bringing the total fatalities to three.
All three car drivers escaped injury.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. Police are working to establish the cause and sequence of events.
Members of the public with information are urged to contact the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at Ipoh district police headquarters.
1183824af588413b: PETALING JAYA: Enam warga asing dituduh tanpa kehadiran mereka di Mahkamah Sesyen Kuala Lumpur semalam atas pertuduhan melakukan samun berkumpulan menggunakan senjata sebuah kondominium mewah di Jalan Ampang membabitkan kerugian RM2.91 juta.
Ketua Polis Kuala Lumpur, Fadil Marsus, berkata mereka didakwa atas kesalahan melakukan samun berkumpulan menggunakan senjata di bawah Seksyen 395 dan 397 Kanun Keseksaan.
Jika sabit kesalahan, mereka boleh dipenjara sehingga 20 tahun dan disebat.
Fadil berkata, pihak pendakwaan telah memohon mahkamah mengeluarkan waran tangkap terhadap enam lelaki itu, dengan tarikh sebutan kes ditetapkan pada 16 Okt ini.
"Pihak polis akan meneruskan proses permohonan Notis Merah melalui Interpol bagi mengesan dan memburu semua suspek terbabit," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Sekumpulan lelaki bertopeng, bersarung tangan dan bersenjatakan pisau memecah masuk sebuah unit kediaman di Pavilion Embassy, Jalan Ampang, antara 2 hingga 3 petang 7 Sept lalu.
Mereka melarikan wang tunai, barang kemas, jam tangan mewah dan pasport seorang warga China berusia 28 tahun, selain merosakkan sebuah telefon bimbit.
55975f7c893ce86c: KOHAT, Sept 19 — The death toll from an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan rose to at least 31, including 16 police personnel, a senior police official told AFP on Saturday, with fighting still ongoing.
Attackers stormed the Old Police Lines complex in Kohat, a town of around 220,000 people in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, on Friday afternoon.
The police compound serves as a district-level police headquarters, housing key offices of the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), Special Branch and several other police units.
“At least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, have been killed and more than 100 injured so far in the militant attack and suicide bombing,” the official said.
“Several militants are still holed up in the Special Branch section of the Kohat Police Complex,” the police official told AFP on condition of anonymity.
“An exchange of fire with them has been ongoing since late last night. Their exact number remains unclear,” the official added.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Pakistani soldiers stand amid rubble at the police headquarters in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, on September 18, 2026, after a militant attack that killed at least 31 people and injured more than 100. — AFP pic
A statement from the Kohat district health officer late on Friday said more than 100 people had been injured, the vast majority of them police personnel, with several in critical condition.
Local militant group Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a faction linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) – the Pakistani Taliban – has claimed responsibility for the attack.
Rubble, blown-out walls
AFP images showed military personnel standing by piles of bricks, rubble and blown-out walls following the attack, with soldiers carrying assault rifles guarding the complex.
Several ambulances were seen lining a street near the police compound.
Pakistan has blamed the increase in attacks in KP and the southern border province of Balochistan on militancy emanating from Afghanistan, where the Taliban government denies Afghan involvement.
The accusations have sparked a bitter rift and armed conflict between the neighbouring countries, and Pakistan has carried out deadly airstrikes it says target militants on Afghan soil.
The Taliban government in Kabul and the United Nations said dozens of civilians were killed in the latest Pakistani strikes on eastern Afghanistan in June.

Ambulances gather near the police headquarters in Kohat, Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, on September 18, 2026, following a militant attack that killed at least 31 people and injured more than 100. — AFP pic
Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack on Friday evening, expressing “deep sorrow and regret over the injury of several people as a result of the blast”.
He directed the “best medical assistance be provided to the injured” and called for a report into the attack.
President Asif Ali Zardari expressed “regret” over the casualties, sending his “best wishes for the speedy recovery of those injured in the blast”.
“The complete elimination of Fitna-al-Khawarij and terrorists operating with foreign backing is essential for national security,” he said, using another term for the TTP group. — AFP
03b56e868c17721c: PETALING JAYA: Dua kenderaan berlogo Jabatan Penjara Malaysia dilihat memasuki kediaman bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak di Langgak Duta, pagi tadi.
Perkembangan itu menyusul pengampunan bersyarat diperoleh bekas presiden Umno untuk menjalani baki hukuman penjara secara tahanan rumah.
Kereta dipercayai membawa beberapa pegawai Jabatan Penjara antara dilihat memasuki pekarangan kediaman itu sejak 9.40 pagi, lapor Berita Harian.
Kehadiran pegawai berkenaan dipercayai bagi menilai kesesuaian kediaman itu dijadikan lokasi Najib menjalani tahanan di rumah.
Beberapa pegawai kemudian dilihat meninjau kawasan sekitar kediaman berkenaan selama kira-kira 15 minit sebelum kembali memasuki pekarangan premis.
Pegawai Khas Najib, Ahmad Lutfi Azhar, ketika ditemui enggan mengulas mengenai kehadiran pegawai terbabit.
Kumpulan petugas media turut berada di sekitar kediaman berkenaan sejak awal pagi bagi mengikuti perkembangan terkini susulan keputusan pengampunan bersyarat terhadap Najib.

Semalam, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim, memperkenan pengampunan bersyarat kepada Najib untuk menjalani baki hukuman secara tahanan di rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028, tertakluk kepada pembayaran denda RM50 juta.

Bahagian Hal Ehwal Undang-undang (BHEUU), Jabatan Perdana Menteri memaklumkan keputusan itu dibuat dalam mesyuarat Lembaga Pengampunan Ke-64 bagi Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur, Labuan dan Putrajaya yang diadakan di Istana Negara.
Mengikut pengampunan bersyarat itu, Najib perlu mematuhi semua syarat ditetapkan dan jika gagal berbuat demikian, pengampunan berkenaan terbatal dan perlu meneruskan baki hukuman di penjara.
Najib menjalani hukuman di Penjara Kajang sejak 23 Ogos 2022 selepas Mahkamah Persekutuan mengekalkan sabitan dan hukuman terhadapnya dalam kes penyelewengan RM42 juta dana SRC International Sdn Bhd.
a83b964e5ddc3653: BEIJING, Sept 19 — Drone owners in Beijing flocked to designated buy-back sites this week, looking to sell their devices for as much as possible ahead of an impending citywide ban.
New rules in the Chinese capital ban not just the flying of unmanned aerial vehicles but also their possession or storage, meaning owners have until November 15 to get rid of their drones.
At several authorised buyer sites across the city, AFP witnessed queues of people waiting for staff to appraise their drones and negotiate prices.
All sites had a visible police presence, indicating the sensitivity of the new laws, and most people there did not want to talk to AFP.
At the flagship store for the world’s largest drone maker DJI in Beijing’s business district, around a dozen people queued on Thursday morning hoping to sell their drones back for a reasonable price.

Users can sell devices at approved buy-back points and receive a government subsidy of 30 per cent of the resale value – up to a maximum of 3,000 yuan (RM1,829) – before October 31, and 15 per cent until November 14.
Alternatively, they can recycle them for a subsidy of 200 yuan (RM122), or ship them out of Beijing free of charge.

“I think (the ban) is reasonable. I can understand why the government wants to ensure safety and manage the airspace,” a 48-year-old drone owner surnamed Wu told AFP as he sat in a queue in a DJI store waiting to sell his device.
“After all, Beijing is the capital,” said Wu, who bought his drone six years ago for around 6,000 yuan (RM3,657).
He was hoping to get at least 1,000 yuan (RM610) for the sale, which was what he had been given as a preliminary estimate on the official re-selling app.
Some were not satisfied.
Zhu, 60, who called himself a drone hobbyist, said the buy-back scheme was “robbery”.
“It’s made me lose a lot of money. This is my private property,” he said, adding that he had sold five drones back, losing thousands on the original prices.
“Of course I’m not happy... I’m helpless and furious.”
Zhu added that the large number of drones being bought back had sent prices plummeting by as much as 40 per cent.
Security fears

Airspace safety fears were raised in June when a light aircraft smashed into Beijing’s tallest building, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others, as well as briefly disrupting the flight path into one of the capital’s international airports.
The incident, which was heavily censored, seems to have unsettled Beijing authorities, happening just a few kilometres from the seat of the Chinese government.
Beijing cited a need to “safeguard the security of the capital” when it announced the complete ban on drone possession inside the city.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A technician assembles drones at a company in the Liangping High-tech Zone, a pilot area for developing China’s low-altitude economy, in Chongqing, southwest China, on September 8, 2026, as Beijing prepares to ban drone possession within city limits from November. — AFP pic
Meanwhile, a “low-altitude” expo scheduled to open Thursday in Beijing was abruptly cancelled, with organisers citing control measures from the city government.
Drone owner Wu said he was pleased that the buy-back plan meant he could easily sell his drone – which he said he no longer used much anyway – for a reasonable amount.
“I checked some online selling platforms and found that without the subsidy it would sell for maybe half the price,” he said.
It is difficult to know how many drones will be affected by the move.
There were 3.285 million drones registered nationwide at the end of 2025, according to the Civil Aviation Administration, but it is not necessary to register drone ownership in most of the country.
Online, many Beijingers posted farewells to their drone collections.
“There’s nothing I can do, thanks for your company,” wrote one user on social media platform Xiaohongshu, known as RedNote abroad.
“I hope you can keep roaming the skies in the future.” — AFP
7f8cf85eba47eda5: PETALING JAYA: Two prisons department vehicles arrived at Najib Razak's residence at Taman Duta in Kuala Lumpur this morning, a day after the former prime minister was granted a conditional pardon to serve his remaining jail term under house arrest.
The vehicles ferrying several prisons department officers were seen entering the compound at about 9.40am, Berita Harian reported.
The officers were reportedly there to evaluate whether the residence was suitable for Najib to be placed under house arrest.
Several officers were seen surveying the surroundings for about 15 minutes before entering the front door.

Yesterday, the Prime Minister’s Department announced that following a Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) meeting, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong decided to allow Najib to serve the remainder of a six-year jail sentence in his SRC International case at his home provided he pays his RM50 million fine
Under the conditional pardon, Najib will serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of the fine.

Najib, 73, has been serving a six-year sentence at Kajang prison after the FTPB halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024. The original RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
3b7934c7118bb853: KUALA LUMPUR: The moment of truth finally arrives for the under-fire national men's hockey team when their Asian Games campaign begins on Sunday against lowly Uzbekistan in their Group B opener at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium.

World No. 15 Malaysia are expected to ease past the world No. 45 Central Asian side, but a convincing victory would help build confidence in a tournament that offers the champions a place at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
The Speedy Tigers will then face world No. 25 Oman on Tuesday, followed by world No. 48 Thailand (Sept 24), world No. 12 Pakistan (Sept 26) and world No. 20 China (Sept 28).
Malaysia will be looking to make amends at the Asian Games after finishing last at the recent World Cup, where they had targeted a quarter-final spot.
Coach Brendon Carolan's team are under pressure to deliver and achieve their target of reaching the Asian Games final.
The Speedy Tigers have had an underwhelming season.
Besides finishing last at the World Cup, they also failed to meet their target at the Nations Cup in South Africa, where they finished fifth.
Malaysia have never won Asian Games gold, with their best results being silver medals in 2010 (Guangzhou) and 2018 (Jakarta).
Carolan's first task is to guide the team into the final before they turn their attention to earning the Olympic berth.
Malaysia have not qualified for the Olympics since Sydney 2000.
Sunday's match will be Malaysia's first against Uzbekistan in a tournament, and Carolan's men need a convincing victory to gain confidence ahead of tougher matches.
Group B's semi-final places are expected to be contested among Pakistan, Malaysia, and China, who are coached by Australian Anthony Farry.
Former national player Maninderjit Singh said the Speedy Tigers were yet to recover from their defeat by Japan at the 2018 Asian Games.
"This year will determine whether we recover or fall further towards an irreparable state on the world stage.
"India and Pakistan are expected to be the leading contenders for Asian Games gold, given that they participated in the recent Pro League and finished higher than Malaysia at the recent World Cup.
"Hosts Japan and South Korea could also upset the form book."
Tomorrow's fixtures
Group A: India vs Indonesia (2pm), Japan vs Sri Lanka (4pm)
Group B: Malaysia vs Uzbekistan (12pm), Pakistan vs Thailand (6pm)
* Malaysian time

d7ee97ff48ffed6d: ISTANBUL: Grid elektrik nasional Cuba terputus sepenuhnya pada Jumaat menyebabkan seluruh negara bergelap ketika berdepan krisis tenaga, menurut Kesatuan Elektrik Cuba (UNE), lapor Anadolu Ajansi.
"Sistem Elektrik Nasional mengalami gangguan sepenuhnya. Protokol pemulihan sedang diaktifkan," kata UNE menerusi platform X.
Syarikat utiliti itu memaklumkan siasatan segera sedang dijalankan bagi mengenal pasti punca gangguan dan perkembangan usaha memulihkan sistem akan dikemas kini.

Ini gangguan terbaharu dalam siri kegagalan bekalan elektrik di seluruh Cuba tahun ini, ketika infrastruktur tenaga negara itu yang semakin usang berdepan kekurangan bahan api dan kapasiti penjanaan terhad.
Cuba mengalami beberapa gangguan bekalan elektrik di seluruh negara Julai lalu, selain satu lagi gangguan besar pada 2 Ogos lepas, menurut pihak berkuasa dan laporan media antarabangsa.
Gangguan pada Jumaat kejadian terbaharu yang menyaksikan grid elektrik nasional negara itu lumpuh sepenuhnya.

Ia berlaku selepas kekurangan bekalan elektrik berpanjangan di Havana dan beberapa kawasan lain, dengan sesetengah bahagian ibu negara dilaporkan mengalami gangguan melebihi 30 jam sejak beberapa minggu ini.
Sistem tenaga Cuba terjejas akibat keadaan loji janakuasa terma semakin merosot, kekurangan bahan api serta kesukaran mengekalkan kapasiti penjanaan elektrik.
Kementerian Tenaga dan Galian sebelum ini mengaitkan gangguan bekalan elektrik dengan gabungan faktor infrastruktur semakin usang, kekurangan bahan api dan masalah dalam sistem penjanaan elektrik.
Sumber tenaga boleh baharu membantu menambah kapasiti penjanaan, namun loji janakuasa terma masih menjadi komponen utama sistem bekalan elektrik Cuba.

Kerajaan Cuba menyalahkan langkah dan sekatan Amerika Syarikat yang menjejaskan bekalan bahan api sebagai faktor memburukkan krisis tenaga, manakala Washington pula mengaitkan masalah ekonomi dan infrastruktur negara itu dengan dasar kerajaan Cuba.
1200c4246645e104: KUCHING: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry will prioritise fertility programmes and treatment aid to tackle low birth rates, particularly in Sarawak and Penang.
Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the initiatives include assisting couples facing fertility issues and encouraging younger couples to start families.
She said while these efforts are already implemented through the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), the ministry intends to sharpen its focus on such programmes next year.
"Sarawak and Penang are among the states that need attention because we want to help boost birth rates," she told reporters after launching the Perantis Pendaya 2.0 initiative.
Nancy added that the assistance includes coverage for treatments such as in vitro fertilisation (IVF) conducted under LPPKN.
"We recognise that economic factors influence young couples' decisions to have children, but the government is addressing these issues," she said.
Nancy said the ministry wants to expand programmes that encourage family growth as the country needs population growth.
She said that the ministry has researched fertility rates to identify appropriate strategies to raise birth numbers.
"At present, the growth rate has not reached the levels we hope for, but we are actively working to promote higher birth rates.
"The research highlights specific factors behind the lower rates, and I will share these findings in due course," she said.
ef7a12625e4928b7: PETALING JAYA: Six foreigners were charged in absentia at the Kuala Lumpur sessions court yesterday with armed gang robbery at a luxury condominium on Jalan Ampang, involving losses of RM2.91 million
Kuala Lumpur police chief Fadil Marsus said they were charged with gang robbery and armed robbery under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code.
If convicted, they could face up to 20 years in prison and whipping.
Fadil said the prosecution has applied for the court to issue warrants of arrest for the six, with mention fixed for Oct 16.
"Police will apply for a Red Notice to be issued by Interpol to hunt down the suspects," he said in a statement.
A group of masked men wearing gloves and armed with knives broke into a residential unit at Pavilion Embassy on Jalan Ampang between 2pm and 3pm on Sept 7.
They made off with cash, jewellery and luxury watches, and also damaged a mobile phone and stole the passport of a 28-year-old Chinese national.
d0ae5347b093a6c7: KUALA LUMPUR: Auditor General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi has been unanimously elected secretary-general of the Asian Organisation of Supreme Audit Institutions (ASOSAI) for the 2027-2030 term.
She was elected at the organisation's governing board meeting in Astana, Kazakhstan, on Thursday, according to the National Audit Department.
Malaysia will host the ASOSAI secretariat from 2027. It last held the position in 1982, 44 years ago.

"The election of Her Excellency Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi as secretary general reflects the confidence of ASOSAI Governing Board members in her leadership to steer the organisation's strategic direction, particularly in the area of capacity development, research and the exchange of expertise in public sector auditing," the department said in a statement.
"The National Audit Department of Malaysia will assume this responsibility from the National Audit Office of the People's Republic of China."
It said the secretariat will coordinate ASOSAI programmes, support the Governing Board, facilitate communication among members, and oversee the organisation's administration and finances.
During the meeting, Wan Suraya presented a progress report on the ASOSAI Working Group on State-Owned Enterprises Audit (WGSOEA), which Malaysia established and has chaired since 2024.
With members from 34 ASOSAI member countries, WGSOEA is the organisation's second-largest working group.

The working group is developing the first ASOSAI Guidelines on State-Owned Enterprises Audit as a common reference to strengthen the auditing and governance of state-owned enterprises across the region.
The guidelines cover financial, compliance and performance audits of state-owned enterprises and are scheduled to be launched at the 17th ASOSAI Assembly in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, in 2027.

The guidelines cover financial, compliance and performance audits of state-owned enterprises and are scheduled to be launched at the 17th ASOSAI Assembly in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, in 2027.

During the meeting, ASOSAI also expressed its appreciation to Malaysia for its commitment to host the regional workshop, "Performance Audit on Public Works Projects", at the National Audit Academy in October 2026.
The two-week workshop will strengthen the capacity of ASOSAI member institutions to conduct performance audits of public works projects.
The working visit to Kazakhstan also included the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the National Audit Department of Malaysia and the Board of Audit and Inspection of Korea.
The MoU focuses on the exchange of expertise, capacity development, and the use of technology and digital approaches in public sector auditing in both countries.
Wan Suraya also held bilateral meetings with her counterparts from China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Iran and Pakistan.

Malaysia also shared its experience through a country paper entitled "Audit of Sustainable Development Impact Assessment and Public Engagement" at the International Scientific and Practical Conference held on Sept 16, 2026, in conjunction with the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the Supreme Audit Chamber of Kazakhstan.
The meeting, which was also attended by Malaysian Ambassador to Kazakhstan Mohd Adli Abdullah, endorsed the admission of Timor-Leste's Supreme Audit Institution as ASOSAI's 49th member.

b9ce8f0de6b0a1da: KAJANG: Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) telah merakam keterangan Menteri Pertanian dan Keterjaminan Makanan, Mohamad Sabu dan ketua setiausaha (KSU) kementerian itu membabitkan isu kelewatan bekalan baja di Kedah.
Ketua Pesuruhjaya SPRM, Abd Halim Aman, berkata keterangan Mohamad dirakam 16 Sept lalu, manakala KSU sehari sebelum itu.

Setakat ini, jelasnya, 37 saksi telah dipanggil dan keterangan mereka dirakam bagi membantu siasatan yang dimulakan 26 Ogos lalu berhubung pelantikan sebuah syarikat oleh Kementerian Pertanian dan Keterjaminan Makanan (KPKM).
"Siasatan masih berlangsung, namun sudah sampai ke penghujung dan dijangka dapat dimuktamadkan dalam tempoh seminggu atau dua minggu lagi," katanya dalam sidang media di sini.

Beliau berkata, SPRM akan mengambil keterangan beberapa saksi lagi bagi melengkapkan siasatan mengikut Seksyen 471 Kanun Keseksaan berkaitan kesalahan menggunakan dokumen yang diketahui atau dipercayai palsu.
Menurutnya, SPRM setakat ini percaya terdapat unsur jenayah dan isu berkaitan tadbir urus dalam kes itu, namun lebih menumpukan aspek kriminaliti.
"Kita ketepikan dahulu isu tadbir urus kerana kita fokus kepada aspek kriminaliti. Bagaimanapun, saya tidak boleh komen lebih daripada itu kerana penyiasatan masih berlangsung."
Sebelum ini, siasatan awal SPRM mendapati sebuah syarikat sepatutnya membekalkan 616,015 beg baja, tetapi hanya 333,655 beg baja dibekalkan sehingga bulan ini, kekurangan 282,360 beg.

Kertas siasatan dibuka selepas menerima aduan berhubung dakwaan kegagalan syarikat pembekal baja dilantik KPKM untuk membekal baja menerusi Skim Insentif Pengeluaran Padi (SIPP) di kawasan Lembaga Kemajuan Pertanian Muda.
4778c577f46f7b4b: WASHINGTON: US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent plans to discuss AI, trade, rare earths and economic issues when he meets with Chinese vice-premier He Lifeng in New York City this weekend, according to a source familiar with his plans.

The discussions are significant because the US and China are the two major forces driving development of advanced AI tools and the global adoption of the technology. Rare earths play a crucial role in the manufacturing of technology.

Bessent, US trade representative Jamieson Greer and He will meet on Sunday in New York ahead of a summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sept 24 in Washington, Greer's office said in a statement.

"The Trump Administration will continue to pursue balanced trade with China by monitoring the implementation of recent commitments, optimizing trade in non-sensitive goods, and improving market access for American farmers, manufacturers, and workers," Greer said in the statement.

Bessent said in a separate statement that he expects the discussions to cover "both open- and closed-weight models." Open-weight models are AI systems with publicly accessible core elements. Users can download and fine-tune them for specific tasks.
Chinese open-weight models are becoming more popular with US companies because they can be cheaper than closed-weight AI tools such as those developed by Anthropic, OpenAI and other US companies.

Chinese AI models have even been used by the US government. Reuters reported on Thursday that a US government website employed an AI model from a Chinese company to allow users to search proposed federal regulations even though the FBI accused the model's developer, Alibaba, of "malicious" copying of Anthropic's technology.

"The United States remains the leader in AI. And we are open to discussions on avoiding shared risks and avoiding bifurcation of our two systems," Bessent said in his statement regarding the China talks.
Bessent has called for the US and China to agree on AI "guardrails" aimed at keeping powerful models out of the hands of malign non-state actors.

Questioned on AI safety at a House of Representatives Financial Services Committee hearing on Tuesday, Bessent said it was up to US AI firms to decide whether to slow their development, but argued they should be held liable for what they build and generate as a safety measure.
Broad discussions

Details about the meetings in New York, which are expected to explore possible areas for Trump and Xi to agree on, have been scant. The source said that the Sunday meetings could extend to Monday on a "working" level, and that the agenda would stay flexible to allow for broad discussion.

Other key topics for Bessent and He to discuss are expected to include potential extension of a tariff truce that expires on Nov 10, and improving flows of Chinese-produced rare-earth magnets and critical minerals that China severely curtailed last year as tariffs on both sides escalated.

Under that truce, China promised to restore the flow of critical minerals to US and global users. However, a senior US official told reporters on Friday that China's performance on that "has not been up to par" and would be a topic for discussion ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
The Trump administration also wants to see China take stronger action to curb the flow of fentanyl precursor chemicals into the US, the official said.

The US-China truce also capped tariffs imposed during Trump's second term in office at about 20%. The Supreme Court later struck down Trump's tariffs invoked under a national emergencies law, including duties related to fentanyl trafficking. Trump's administration has been rebuilding them under new authorities.

The US has restored a 12.5% tariff on Chinese goods over forced labour allegations and is finalising a separate tariff investigation aimed at curbing excess industrial capacity that it says is rampant in China.
At a Trump-Xi meeting in May, China pledged to increase purchases of US agriculture products and at least 200 Boeing aircraft, but details on those transactions have yet to emerge.

With only short preparation time, expectations for Bessent and He to arrange major new deals from the Trump-Xi summit are low, said Wendy Cutler, policy director for the Asia Society in Washington, adding that both sides have an interest in keeping trade tensions from flaring up again.
"If anything, it's an exercise in kind of managing the relationship and ensuring that the elements in the truce are actually being lived up to," Cutler said.

Also in May, the US and China agreed to launch discussions to reduce tariffs for non-strategic goods under a so-called "Board of Trade" mechanism along with a similar forum to deal with specific investment issues.

While the Trump administration has tightened restrictions on American companies investing in some industries in China, Reuters reported on Friday that it is working on rules that would likely allow US pharmaceutical firms to invest in promising Chinese drugs and strike licensing deals for them.
China's commerce ministry said on Saturday that He would also lead a delegation of Chinese companies to the US to hold economic and trade consultations ahead of the summit.

The business delegation, which mirrors a group of American CEOs that Trump brought to Beijing May, comes as Trump expresses openness to Chinese automakers building US factories. US auto industry groups on Friday urged Trump to maintain an effective ban on Chinese vehicle sales in the US on national security grounds.
ba515959a40725ab: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission says it has completed its investigation into allegations of misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, linked to Felda and its investment arm, Felda Investment Corporation (FIC).

MACC chief commissioner Abd Halim Aman said statements from 30 witnesses, including Felda board members and management, had been recorded in connection with the KLVC investigation, which has now been completed, Bernama reported.
He said a former Felda director-general and a former FIC chief executive officer were arrested last Sunday.
“MACC will recommend that charges be brought against the two individuals based on the investigation papers,” he told a press conference in Kajang today.
"We will seek the Attorney General’s Chambers’ consent to proceed with the prosecution and other related matters."
Halim said former Felda chairman Isa Samad had his statement taken by MACC at the Sungai Buloh prison on Thursday.
The statement was recorded in connection with seven investigations into alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving investments at Felda and FIC.
“The statement was recorded at Sungai Buloh prison on Sept 17. It is expected to continue next week.

“As of Sept 18, a total of 34 witnesses have been called and their statements recorded in connection with the seven cases being investigated by MACC. They include former Felda board members and former FIC board members," he said.
The investigations, dubbed Op Fella by the anti-graft agency, are focused on investment transactions and asset acquisitions by Felda and FIC over a 10-year period from 2010.

Bernama also reported that MACC has recorded statements from agriculture and food security minister Mohamad Sabu and the ministry’s secretary-general in connection with an investigation into the delays in the supply of fertiliser in Kedah.
Halim said Mohamad’s statement was recorded on Sept 16, and the secretary-general’s statement a day earlier.

So far, 37 witnesses had been called and their statements recorded to assist in the investigation, which began on Aug 26, regarding the appointment of a company by the agriculture and food security ministry.
“The investigation is ongoing, and is expected to be finalised within a week or two,” Halim said.

ba8d127bb9dc4c0e: PETALING JAYA: Bersatu menuntut kerajaan memastikan prinsip layanan sama rata diterapkan dalam pelaksanaan tahanan di rumah, termasuk menjelaskan sama ada kemudahan itu boleh dipertimbangkan bagi banduan lain yang memenuhi kriteria ditetapkan.

Setiausaha Agung, Azmin Ali, berkata kerajaan wajar menjelaskan kerangka undang-undang, tatacara dan kriteria pelaksanaan tahanan rumah supaya tidak timbul persepsi wujud layanan berbeza berdasarkan kedudukan atau pengaruh seseorang.
“Termasuk sama ada keistimewaan yang sama boleh dipertimbangkan secara adil kepada banduan lain yang memenuhi kriteria ditetapkan.
"Penjelasan ini penting supaya tidak timbul persepsi bahawa terdapat satu bentuk layanan bagi golongan bangsawan, berpengaruh dan satu lagi bagi rakyat biasa," katanya dalam kenyataan.

Azmin berkata, rakyat berhak mendapat keyakinan bahawa kedudukan, pengaruh atau latar belakang seseorang tidak mewujudkan piawaian pelaksanaan hukuman berbeza daripada yang terpakai kepada rakyat biasa.

Beliau berkata, penjelasan mengenai semua syarat dikenakan terhadap bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak, termasuk menjalani baki hukuman secara tahanan di rumah, perlu diumumkan secara terperinci bagi menjamin ketelusan.
Katanya, Bersatu juga menghormati Perkara 42 Perlembagaan Persekutuan yang memperuntukkan Yang di-Pertuan Agong mempunyai kuasa untuk memberi ampun, menunda atau legakan hukuman.
"Kuasa pengampunan Yang di-Pertuan Agong di bawah Perkara 42 terpakai kepada semua banduan yang berhak memohon pengampunan melalui proses undang-undang," katannya.

Semalam, Jabatan Perdana Menteri (JPM) mengumumkan Najib diberikan pengampunan bersyarat dan dibenarkan menjalani baki hukuman penjara enam tahun di kediamannya, dengan syarat membayar denda RM50 juta secara penuh.
Bekas presiden Umno itu akan dibenarkan menjalani baki hukumannya bagi kes SRC International di bawah tahanan di rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028.

Agong mengurniakan pengampunan bersyarat kepada Najib susulan mesyuarat Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan, yang turut dianggotai peguam negara, menteri Wilayah Persekutuan dan tiga ahli dilantik oleh Seri Paduka Baginda.

Najib, 73, sedang menjalani hukuman penjara enam tahun di Penjara Kajang selepas hukuman asalnya selama 12 tahun dikurangkan separuh pada Februari 2024. Denda asal sebanyak RM210 juta turut dikurangkan kepada RM50 juta.
Beliau mula dipenjarakan pada Ogos 2022 selepas Mahkamah Persekutuan menolak rayuan akhirnya dalam kes itu.
Pada Disember 2025, Najib disabitkan atas kesalahan salah guna kuasa dan pengubahan wang haram membabitkan lebih RM2 bilion berkaitan 1MDB.
Bekas Ahli Parlimen Pekan itu dijatuhi hukuman penjara 15 tahun dan denda RM11.38 bilion, dan kini sedang merayu sabitan tersebut.

cfeb97f10732775e: PETALING JAYA: Bekas pemimpin DAP, Ong Kian Ming berkata parti itu wajar memberi kata dua kepada Perdana Menteri, Anwar Ibrahim dan mendesaknya menyingkirkan Umno daripada Jemaah Menteri selepas bekas perdana menteri, Najib Razak mendapat pengampunan bersyarat.

Jelasnya, DAP perlu menuntut Anwar menyingkirkan Umno daripada Jemaah Menteri sebelum mesyuarat seterusnya untuk menunjukkan keseriusan Pakatan Harapan menolak tindakan Umno berusaha mendapatkan pengampunan bagi Najib serta mengumpul dana bagi membayar denda RM50 juta bekas presidennya.

Ong berkata, kata dua itu perlu disertakan tarikh akhir mesyuarat Jemaah Menteri atau ia sekadar kenyataan dangkal dan bukannya ancaman berwibawa.

Menurutnya, tidak adil menyalahkan Menteri Wilayah Persekutuan, Hannah Yeoh yang menganggotai Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan kerana keputusan pengampunan merupakan hak prerogatif Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

"Jika ada yang patut letak jawatan segera, orang itu mungkin ialah Nga Kor Ming yang pernah berkata dalam satu wawancara sebelum PRN Johor bahawa beliau akan melepaskan jawatan menteri jika BN menang besar di Johor dan Najib dibebaskan."

Ong berkata, DAP juga boleh mengugut akan menarik sokongan terhadap kerajaan secara keseluruhan, tetapi langkah itu mungkin membawa kepada pembubaran Parlimen kerana Barisan Nasional dijangka melakukan perkara sama untuk Anwar hilang sokongan majoriti.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, tindakan itu lebih berisiko kerana boleh menggugat asas PH dan menimbulkan persoalan sama ada DAP wajar terus kekal dalam gabungan berkenaan.

"Adakah ini akan menyebabkan penilaian semula terhadap kemungkinan pakatan pilihan raya antara BN dan PN menjelang PRU akan datang?" soalnya.
9d9e9c7de8f7cc19: BEIJING: Drone owners in Beijing flocked to designated buy-back sites this week, looking to sell their devices for as much as possible ahead of an impending citywide ban.
New rules in the Chinese capital ban not just the flying of unmanned aerial vehicles but the possession or storage of them, meaning owners have until November 15 to get rid of their drones.
At several authorised buyer sites across the city, AFP witnessed queues of people waiting for staff to appraise their drones and negotiate prices.
All sites had a visible police presence, indicating the sensitivity of the new laws, and most people there did not want to talk to AFP.
At the flagship store for the world's largest drone maker DJI in Beijing's business district, around a dozen people queued on Thursday morning hoping to sell their drones back for a reasonable price.

Users can sell devices at approved buy-back points and receive a government subsidy of 30 percent of the resale value — up to a maximum of 3,000 yuan (nearly US$450) — before Oct 31, and of 15 per cent until Nov 14.
Alternatively, they can recycle them for a subsidy of 200 yuan, or ship them out of Beijing free of charge.

"I think (the ban) is reasonable. I can understand why the government wants to ensure safety and manage the airspace," a 48-year-old drone owner surnamed Wu told AFP as he sat in a queue in a DJI store waiting to sell his device.
"After all, Beijing is the capital," said Wu, who bought his drone six years ago for around 6,000 yuan.
He was hoping to get at least 1,000 yuan for the sale, which was what he had been given as a preliminary estimate on the official re-selling app.
Some were not satisfied.
Zhu, 60, who called himself a drone hobbyist, said the buy-back scheme was "robbery."
"It's made me lose a lot of money. This is my private property," he said, adding that he had sold five drones back, losing thousands on the original prices.
"Of course I'm not happy... I'm helpless and furious."
Zhu added that the large number of drones being bought back had sent prices plummeting as much as 40 percent.
- Security fears -

Airspace safety fears were raised in June when a light aircraft smashed into Beijing's tallest building, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others – as well as briefly disrupting the flight path into one of the capital's international airports.
The incident, which was heavily censored, seems to have unsettled Beijing authorities, happening just a few kilometres (miles) from the seat of the Chinese government.
Beijing cited a need to "safeguard the security of the capital" when it announced the complete ban on drone possession inside the city.
Meanwhile, a "low-altitude" expo scheduled to open Thursday in Beijing was abruptly cancelled, with organisers citing control measures from the city government.
Drone owner Wu said he was pleased that the buy-back plan meant he could easily sell his drone — which he said he no longer used much anyway — for a reasonable amount.
"I checked some online selling platforms and found that without the subsidy it would sell for maybe half the price", he said.
It is difficult to know how many drones will be affected by the move.
There were 3.285 million drones registered nationwide at the end of 2025, according to the Civil Aviation Administration, but it is not necessary to register drone ownership in most of the country.
Online, many Beijingers posted farewells to their drone collections.
"There's nothing I can do, thanks for your company," wrote one user on social media platform Xiaohongshu, known as RedNote abroad.
"I hope you can keep roaming the skies in the future." — AFP
