a11deedd751acec1: KUALA LUMPUR: Ahmad Tea marked its 40th anniversary with a Ruby Jubilee celebration in Malaysia on Thursday, unveiling its Sencha tea and announcing footballer Antoine Semenyo as its global brand ambassador.
The event looked back on the family-owned British company's beginnings in Southampton, England, and its growth into a business whose products are available in more than 80 markets.
Founded in 1986 by Rahim Afshar and his brothers, Ahmad Tea began with a small family tea shop.
According to the company, the brothers set out to make tea they would be happy to serve in their own home, a principle it says continues to guide the business.
Their range has since grown to include classic British black teas, herbal infusions and other varieties. The introduction of Sencha adds to that range as the company enters its fifth decade.
Consequently, Semenyo's appointment is tied to Ahmad Tea's global 'Preparation Is Everything' campaign, which echoes the importance of preparation, discipline and consistency in achieving excellence.
This philosophy is shared by both the brand and Semenyo, who believe that getting small details right are vital to attaining exceptional results.
The Ruby Jubilee event included a display tracing Ahmad Tea's 40-year history, tea-tasting sessions and a presentation of its products.
Ahmad Tea is represented in Malaysia by Sangla Foods Sdn Bhd, a local food and beverage distributor founded in 1993.
6a91ae701b1c119b: PETALING JAYA: Bersatu has urged the government to reveal all the house arrest conditions imposed on former prime minister Najib Razak as part of his conditional pardon in his SRC International case.
Bersatu secretary-general Azmin Ali said these terms should be revealed in detail to Malaysians given the questions and concerns that arose following the pardon decision.
"It is important to reveal these details to avoid public anger and unrest that could threaten the integrity of the judiciary and public confidence in our legal system," he said in a statement.
Azmin said the government should explain the legal framework, procedures, and criteria for house arrests, and whether other inmates could apply for the same "privilege".

He maintained that Bersatu's stand is that those convicted of corruption should be punished according to the law and the Federal Constitution, but Article 42 of the constitution accords the king with the power of pardon.
"However, Bersatu understands the questions that have risen among the people regarding the principle of equality before the law.
"The people deserve to have the confidence that one's position, influence, or background should not provide for a separate set of punishments," he said.

Yesterday, the Prime Minister’s Department announced that following a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting, the king decided to allow Najib to serve the remainder of a six-year jail sentence at his home provided he pays his RM50 million fine in his SRC International case.
Under the conditional pardon, Najib will serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of the fine.

Najib, 73, has been serving a six-year sentence at Kajang prison after the board halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024. The original RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
aad67fe17c3436b9: SEOUL: South Korean president Lee Jae Myung's nominee for justice minister withdrew from consideration on Saturday, the second of Lee's cabinet picks to step aside this month as his approval ratings slump.
Kim Seung-won's exit follows the withdrawal of Yong Hye-in as nominee for gender-equality minister on Sunday, in the latest fallout from Lee's cabinet reshuffle in late August.

Kim, who said he did not want to add any burden to Lee's administration, criticised a conservative lawmaker who had accused him of lobbying regulators over a drug trial and of financial irregularities. Kim has denied the allegations.
"I gravely accept that I did not meet the public's expectations, and I will deeply reflect on my shortcomings," Kim told a press conference.

A Gallup Korea poll released on Friday put Lee's public approval at 37%, the lowest since he took office in June 2025, a decline pollsters have partly linked to criticism over his personnel appointments.
At a press conference on Friday, Lee acknowledged shortcomings in his administration's screening of nominees. "We are currently working to reexamine our personnel system," the president said.

7f88af3b46c573e1: LOS ANGELES: Duncan Sheik, the celebrated singer-songwriter behind the 1996 hit single Barely Breathing and the Tony Award-winning composer of Spring Awakening, has died at the age of 56.
His mother, Suzanne, confirmed his passing to The New York Times, saying that the cause of death was organ failure.
According to Rolling Stone, his death follows an unspecified health issue earlier in the week that had left him in a critical but stable condition in hospital.

A statement posted to Sheik's official social media accounts paid tribute to his memory: "It is with profound sadness that we confirm the passing of Duncan Sheik. The world has lost a singular talent, and deeply influential voice in music and theatre."
The post added that the singer would be fondly remembered for "his sensitivity, wit, intelligence, and depth of spirit."
Born in New Jersey, Sheik performed alongside Lisa Loeb whilst studying at Brown University before launching his self-titled debut album in 1996.
The record spawned Barely Breathing, which spent 55 consecutive weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and earned him a Grammy Award nomination for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance.
Although Barely Breathing marked his main commercial chart success, Sheik maintained a prolific recording career, releasing nine studio albums.
His 2001 record Phantom Moon, a tribute to Nick Drake, established a key partnership with poet and lyricist Steven Sater.
The pair subsequently collaborated on the acclaimed 2006 rock musical Spring Awakening, based on an 1891 German play.

The production proved to be a critical triumph, winning Best Musical at the Tony Awards, whilst Sheik earned Tonys for Best Original Score and Best Orchestrations, alongside a Grammy Award for Best Musical Show Album.

Speaking about his bond with Sater, Sheik once remarked, "I think he is a genius. He is 'out there', eccentric and unique, and that's why I love him. I try to make sure my music has those qualities in it."
Over the next two decades, Sheik composed scores for numerous stage productions, including musical adaptations of Alice in Wonderland, The Secret Life of Bees, and American Psycho.
Discussing the latter's 2016 Broadway run, he explained he wanted the production to be "a little deeper and more ambiguous, weird and strange, and, hopefully, beautiful."
At the time of his death, he was preparing for an off-Broadway staging of Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen this autumn, alongside an upcoming revival of Spring Awakening scheduled for November.

Expressing their gratitude following the sad news, Sheik's family said: "We are deeply grateful for the outpouring of love from his fans, friends, collaborators, and the artistic community. His musical legacy will continue to inspire generations to come."

"What are the specific conditions that allow someone to be placed under house arrest? What is the mechanism for the execution of house arrest?
"The people do not want this house arrest to be used merely to satisfy certain political elites," he said in a statement.
Rafique, a lawyer by profession, also pointed out that Article 8 the Federal Constitution provides for equal treatment and protection under the law.

He said granting house arrests without clear, transparent guidelines and conditions could give rise to perceptions of double standards, with the law imposed "comfortably" on elites and more strictly on regular folk.

Yesterday, the Prime Minister’s Department announced that following a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong decided to allow Najib to serve the remainder of a six-year jail sentence at his home provided he pays his RM50 million fine in his SRC International case.
Under the conditional pardon, Najib will serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of the fine.

Najib, 73, has been serving a six-year sentence at Kajang prison after the board halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024. The original RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
eabd6e350011b5cc: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia face a difficult route to the medal rounds in both the men's and women's team badminton competitions at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
The women's team, led by world No. 5 pair Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah, will open their campaign against Hong Kong at Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium on Sunday.
Victory would send Malaysia into the quarter-finals against third seeds South Korea, who received a first-round bye.
Should Malaysia upset the Koreans, they could face second seeds and hosts Japan in the semi-finals for a place in the gold-medal tie.
The men's competition begins on Monday, with Aaron Chia-led Malaysia expected to ease past Mongolia in the opening round.
Victory would set up a stern quarter-final clash against top seeds Indonesia, who were handed a bye into the last eight.
If Malaysia overcome Indonesia, either Taiwan or Thailand could await them in the semi-finals.
At the 2022 Hangzhou edition, Malaysia were eliminated by South Korea in the first round of the men's competition, while the women's team did not compete.
Team manager Datuk Ng Chin Chai said Malaysia would need to overcome strong opposition regardless of their route through the draw.
"There is no easy route to winning a medal as all the top four seeds in both the men's and women's team events are strong," said Chin Chai.
"Malaysia have brought their best available players and prepared well.
'Now is the time for our team to produce their best form and overcome any teams in our path to the podium."
The draw means both Malaysian teams will have to eliminate some of Asia's strongest badminton nations to challenge for gold.
Malaysia's last team medal came at the 2014 Incheon edition, when a Datuk Seri Lee Chong Wei-led team won bronze.
The men's team have won silver medals at the 1966 Bangkok and 1990 Beijing Games, their best performances in the competition.
The Malaysian women have stood on the podium only once, winning silver at the 1962 Jakarta edition after losing to Indonesia in the final.
21807de74c177fb0: KUALA LUMPUR: Two vehicles bearing the Prison Department logo were seen entering former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's residence at Langgak Duta here this morning.
The vehicles, believed to be carrying several Prison Department officers, were seen entering the compound about 9.40am.
It is learnt that the officers were there to assess the suitability of the residence as the location for Najib to serve his house arrest.
Several officers were later seen inspecting the area around the residence for about 15 minutes before re-entering the compound.
The officers were seen leaving the premises about 11.50am.
However, Najib's special officer, Ahmad Lutfi Azhar, declined to comment when met at the residence.
About 10 media personnel have also been stationed outside the residence since this morning to follow the latest developments following the decision to grant Najib a conditional pardon.

It was reported yesterday that Najib was granted house arrest for the remainder of his sentence on condition that he pays the RM50 million fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.

The Federal Territories Pardons Board, in a statement, had said that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
It also said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
670473704e58aa73: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 19 — A 55-year-old woman who went to the Sabah National Registration Department (NRD) to replace her identity card ended up being arrested after the card was found to be fake.

Jamilah Akrim was sentenced to four months’ jail by Magistrate Dzul Elmy Yunus after pleading guilty to possessing the fake identity card at the Sabah NRD Identity Card Division at about 11.30am on Sept 10.
The court also ordered Jamilah to be referred to the Immigration Department for further action upon completing her sentence.

The court heard that Jamilah presented the card when seeking a replacement, but checks by NRD officers found it did not exist in the department’s records, while her thumbprints also did not match any records in the system.

She was charged under Regulation 25(1)(e) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 (Amendment 2007), which carries up to three years’ jail or a fine of up to RM20,000, or both, upon conviction. — Daily Express
b2dedae5b03901b9: SEOUL: North Korea dismissed a UN atomic watchdog resolution that renewed demands to halt nuclear activities, saying it has "no effect" because Pyongyang is not an IAEA member, state media reported Saturday.

A foreign ministry statement on Friday accused "hostile forces" of seeking to bring an end to the country's nuclear program during this week's general conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency, state news agency KCNA said.

"Pitifully, the 'resolution' cooked up by the US and the West has no effect on the DPRK's position as a nuclear weapons state," a foreign ministry spokesman said, referring to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, its official name.

"The DPRK has not been a member of the NPT and the IAEA from long ago and, therefore, it is illegal and the height of impudence to talk about the position of our state and its efforts to bolster up the defence capabilities," the spokesman added.

"The DPRK's position as a nuclear weapons state does not need the recognition of the US, the West and the IAEA. It is guaranteed by the actual nuclear deterrent and irreversibly and permanently fixed by the supreme law of the state."
North Korea has legally enshrined its status as a nuclear weapons state, with its leadership declaring the country's atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.

In the statement, the ministry spokesman said the DPRK was positioned to "more offensively implement its strategic and long-term plans for building reliable self-defensive deterrent to cope with the ever-worsening international security environment."
US President Donald Trump said in August that Pyongyang possesses 57 "very powerful" nuclear weapons, with Seoul putting the figure at between 80 and 120.
The US leader has expressed a willingness to resume dialogue with Kim Jong Un, saying last month that he planned to meet him later this year.
In a separate statement on Thursday, Kim's powerful sister said the country's nuclear-armed status was "absolute", and called those hoping for its denuclearisation "idiots".
7b0da61504df85b2: PETALING JAYA: Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) menyerahkan notis kepada bekas pengerusi Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim dan ahli keluarganya termasuk anak-anak untuk mengisytiharkan harta.
Ketua Pesuruhjaya SPRM, Abd Halim Aman, berkata notis itu disampaikan kepada Azeez dan ahli keluarga terdekatnya mengikut peruntukan undang-undang.
“Pihak kami telah menyerahkan notis kepada Azeez dan ahli keluarganya untuk beliau mengisytiharkan hartanya seperti yang termaktub di bawah undang-undang.

“Di bawah akta itu tempohnya sebulan. Kalau contohnya masa dan tempoh sebulan itu tidak mencukupi, pihak kami akan memberikan lanjutan tertakluk kepada keadaan,” katanya dalam sidang media program menembak bersama media 2026 di Lapang Sasar Maktab Penjara Kajang, menurut Kosmo.

Pada 9 Sept lalu, Azeez mengaku tidak bersalah di Mahkamah Sesyen Kuala Lumpur atas satu pertuduhan menggunakan kedudukannya untuk mendapatkan jawatan pengerusi Putrajaya Perdana Berhad serta meyakinkan ahli Lembaga TH meluluskan cadangan pelaburan RM193.5 juta dalam syarikat itu.

Sebelum itu, Azeez turut ditahan bagi membantu siasatan berhubung kes berkaitan pemberian hibah TH mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan sebelum dibebaskan selepas permohonan polis untuk melanjutkan remannya ditolak mahkamah.
Pendakwaan itu adalah sebahagian tindakan susulan pihak berkuasa terhadap penemuan laporan Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja (RCI) berhubung pengurusan serta operasi TH
Sementara itu, Halim berkata setakat semalam seramai enam individu didakwa berhubung lapan isu atau kes disiasat susulan laporan RCI TH.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, siasatan SPRM belum berakhir apabila terdapat lima lagi masih berlangsung dan belum dimuktamadkan.
ce14393dd67471b9: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The constitutional power to grant pardons should not be portrayed as placing any individual above the law, Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today.
She said the power of pardon was expressly provided for under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution and was therefore not a power exercised outside the law.
“The principle of the rule of law is not in dispute. No individual, government or institution is above the law.
“However, the Federal Constitution is the supreme law of the country, and all parties are likewise bound by its provisions,” she said in a statement posted on her Facebook page.
Azalina was responding to a statement by the Pakatan Harapan Presidential Council yesterday following the conditional royal pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

She said judicial decisions and the pardoning process were distinct matters, with the courts responsible for determining guilt and sentences, while Article 42 provides a constitutional mechanism for pardons, reprieves and remissions of sentences.
“The existence of the constitutional power of pardon does not mean that a court’s decision is disregarded, nor does it place any individual above the law,” she said.
She added that every institution must act within the powers conferred on it by the Federal Constitution.

“The respective roles of the Pardons Board, the Attorney General and the relevant Minister must be understood in accordance with Article 42 and the prescribed constitutional process, rather than through political interpretation or perception,” she said.

Azalina said questions concerning the validity, legal effect or process of any action should be assessed based on the Constitution, the facts and the actual process followed rather than merely on political statements.
“Respect the decisions of the courts. Respect the Constitution. Respect the processes provided for by the Constitution.
“No one is above the law. And no one is above the Constitution,” she added.

Najib was convicted in 2020 over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International, a former 1MDB subsidiary, and began serving his 12-year prison sentence in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction.
His original sentence was halved to six years and his RM210 million fine reduced to RM50 million following a review by the Federal Territories Pardons Board in 2024.

Yesterday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with conditions that have not been publicly disclosed so far.
6cf38ac6c00acc40: Demonstrators gathered outside the building in Washington, after the president was spotted holding a placard that read: ‘Kennedy Center DEMOLIS ...’ On Friday evening thousands of protesters gathered outside the Kennedy Center in view of the marble facade that remained concealed by scaffolding and tarpaulins, to protest Donald Trump’s plans for the facility and express alarm that he might make good on his threat to tear down the institution. Crowding streets in the Foggy Bottom area of Washington and locking down traffic as they walked, many carried signs, as they joined in the “Hands Around the Kennedy Center” protest. Some wore costumes and booed when the president was mentioned during the program. Continue reading...
aa87dd32ba4857d6: SYDNEY: Several beaches along the coast of Western Australia, including in the state capital Perth, remained closed on Saturday, a day after a fatal shark attack at a popular beach in the city.
The victim, a male swimmer, died on Friday after being mauled at Sorrento Beach, around 20km from Perth's central business district, prompting the closure of beaches along 30km of coastline.
The local council said in a Facebook post that beaches would remain closed until at least noon on Saturday.
Friday's incident is the latest ‌in a series of shark attacks in Australia and comes after a surfer was bitten in an attack in the same ​state on Monday.
In that attack, a surfer was bitten at a beach in the ​town of Geraldton, around 400km north of ​Perth. ⁠The surfer lost his foot in the attack and suffered serious leg injuries, local media said.
In June a 35-year-old man ⁠was killed while ​spearfishing off the state's south coast, while a 38-year-old man was mauled to death off an island near Perth ​in May.
8603c28030cdbe33: PETALING JAYA: Former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim and his family have been ordered to declare their assets by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission.
MACC chief Abd Halim Aman said asset declaration notices have been served on Azeez and his immediate family, including his children, Kosmo reported.
"Under the law, they have a month (to declare their assets). If that one-month period is insufficient, we could grant an extension.
"It's his immediate family. I can't say how many (have been served with asset declaration notices), but it includes his children," he said.
On Sept 9, Azeez claimed trial to abusing his position as TH chairman to obtain gratification in the form of a chairmanship and other perks in another company.
The position allegedly came with an annual remuneration of RM690,000 and the use of a BMW 7 Series car.

The former Baling MP from Umno was charged in 2019 with accepting bribes amounting to RM5.2 million in connection with road projects in Perak and Kedah, and 10 counts of money laundering involving RM13.9 million.
Four of the money laundering charges were quashed in August 2022 before he was granted a full acquittal in his corruption case in December that year.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers had said it concluded that it did not have any evidence to support the corruption case brought against Azeez after further investigations by MACC.
b30118f6d8070331: KOTA BHARU, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) today assisted with the burial of a 250-kilogramme man at the Gual Tinggi Islamic Cemetery in Rantau Panjang.
Rantau Panjang APM officer Lt (PA) Mohd Fuad Ismail said the team received a request from the Ministry of Health early this morning to undertake the special service.

“The MOH requested assistance to transport the 23-year-old deceased, who was from Kampung Gual Tinggi, Rantau Panjang, and had an obesity-related condition, from Universiti Sains Malaysia Hospital in Kubang Kerian to Masjid Al-Hidayah for the funeral prayer before he was buried.

“The operation lasted nearly five hours, from 11.01 am to 3.56 pm, involving an officer, two personnel, and a lorry. The villagers also lent a hand to facilitate the burial arrangements,” he said in a statement last night. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The initials APM stand for Angkatan Pertahanan Awam Malaysia.
19e76fe9303c367a: PETALING JAYA: The haze situation nationwide has improved with the number of areas recording unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings down to 20 as of 9am, from 32 yesterday evening .
According to the Air Pollutant Index management system (APIMS) portal, Kuching and Serian in Sarawak recorded the highest reading at 169, Bernama reported.
Six other areas in the state also registered unhealthy API levels: Samarahan (163), Sri Aman (162), Sibu (159), Sarikei (152), Bintulu (135) and Kapit (118).
Two areas in Perak logged unhealthy readings: Seri Manjung (164) and Tanjung Malim (113). Over in Selangor, the affected areas are Shah Alam (157), Petaling Jaya (139) and Johan Setia (113).
In addition, two areas in Kuala Lumpur registered unhealthy levels: Batu Muda (155) and Cheras (155), along with Putrajaya (154).
Unhealthy API readings were also recorded in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (151); Larkin, Johor (139); Bukit Rambai, Melaka (111); and Tawau, Sabah (108).
Meanwhile, 37 areas recorded moderate readings, while another 10 areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 301 and above is hazardous.
53b62c1b1feb5cfd: PETALING JAYA: DAP should issue Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim an ultimatum and push for Umno's removal from the Cabinet over the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Najib Razak, says a former party leader.

Ong Kian Ming, a political analyst, said DAP must prove that allowing Najib out of prison was truly a "red line" for the party, especially as supporters will expect DAP to respond to the pardon with concrete action.

Ong said his former party should demand that Anwar boot Umno from the Cabinet before the next Cabinet meeting, to display Pakatan Harapan's seriousness in disagreeing with Umno seeking Najib's pardon and raising funds to pay its former president's RM50 million fine.
"Deputy prime minister and Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi openly challenged Anwar to remove Umno Cabinet members in the past few months.

"This would be the perfect opportunity for Anwar to take up Zahid’s challenge," he said in a Facebook post, adding that the 2027 budget could still be passed without the support of the 30 Barisan Nasional MPs.
Ong said this ultimatum must include the Cabinet meeting deadline or it would only be a superficial statement rather than a credible threat.
The former Bangi MP also said it would make more sense than DAP resigning from the Cabinet.

He said it would be unfair to blame federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh, who sits on the Federal Territories Pardons Board, for carrying out a decision that was ultimately the king's prerogative.

"If anyone should resign immediately, it should probably be Nga Kor Ming, who said in an interview before the Johor polls that he would resign as minister if BN won big in Johor and Najib was freed," he said.

Ong said DAP could also threaten to pull support for the government as a whole, adding that this was highly likely to lead to Parliament's dissolution as BN would be expected to do the same to trigger a loss of majority support for Anwar.
However, he said, this would be a riskier move as it would threaten PH's foundations and even lead to the question of whether DAP should stay in the coalition.

"But if the 1MDB issue and Najib’s house arrest (are) indeed a 'red line' for DAP, then it makes sense for DAP to not just quit the Cabinet but also withdraw from the unity government, if Anwar does not agree to this demand.
"In other words, if DAP wants to issue such an ultimatum, it might as well go all the way so that its supporters are in no doubt about its commitment to this 'red line'," he said.
DAP's central executive committee will meet at 3pm today to decide the party’s position and follow-up action after Najib's conditional pardon.
Ong also warned Umno to tread cautiously in responding to Najib's conditional pardon, reminding the BN lynchpin that the 1MDB scandal was one of the main reasons it fell from power in 2018.
He said Umno should not take Malay support for granted despite its handsome victories in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections.
"What if PAS and Perikatan Nasional sense weakness in Umno's public support because of its insistence on supporting Najib, without admitting to the mistakes made during the 1MDB scandal?
"Would this lead to a rethinking of a possible electoral pact between BN and PN in the upcoming general election?" he said.
15af558e6a926373: MADRID, Sept 19 — Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho admitted his team does not know how to control matches ahead of tomorrow’s La Liga derby clash against Atletico Madrid.

Before the first major test of Mourinho’s second spell at the helm, Los Blancos have shown attacking dynamism the coach called “frenetic”, but the Portuguese veteran acknowledged his team cannot shut the door on opponents.
Madrid trail unbeaten champions Barcelona at the top of the table by three points, after losing one of their six opening games and winning the other five, with Atletico third.
However they needed late strikes by back-up striker Carlos Espi to secure wins at Espanyol and Elche to cling to Barcelona’s tail.
“The problem seems obvious to me. It’s harder to know why, but it’s easy to understand that there are matches that seem over and, in the end, aren’t,” said Mourinho.
“(There are) matches where we have three, four, five chances to finish them and don’t.
“After failing to do so, it feels like we go from ease, because it seemed easy, to losing control.”
Wily Atletico coach Diego Simeone will aim to punish Madrid if they take their eye off the ball in the derby.
Mourinho said his team’s defensive issues were of concern for that game and beyond.
“Not just for tomorrow’s match, but for every match. I like my team to score goals... but I also like controlling matches,” explained Mourinho.
“I don’t like gifting control. It’s not about the goals, it’s about giving away control of the match.”

Bernardo Silva is likely to start against Atletico after being rested against Elche on Tuesday, which could help Madrid take a firmer grip on the game, although Mourinho’s squad does not seem ideally equipped to control matches despite a lavish summer spending spree.
“We’re a frenetic side, who gets the ball back and accelerates,” said Mourinho.

Madrid’s team is defined by their star attacking trio of Vinicius Junior, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham, which effectively ensures they will play at great pace, regardless of the scenario, which can leave them exposed at the back.
Ceuta shirt fallout

Vinicius Junior is often jeered by Atletico Madrid fans and that could be exacerbated in tomorrow’s away trip after the forward, along with team-mates Kylian Mbappe and Ibrahima Konate, did not fully wear a t-shirt supporting the people of Ceuta.
The Madrid trio partially obscured a message on the shirt reading “we are all Ceutans”, regarding the Spanish territory in north Africa affected by a migration crisis with Morocco.
La Liga president Javier Tebas criticised the three players on Wednesday for not wearing the shirt properly ahead of Madrid’s late win against Elche.
Mbappe said his decision to roll up the shirt was to make a gesture in support of immigrants who had lost their lives while trying to cross the border, but also supported Ceutans.
Vinicius has been whistled by his own fans in recent weeks for poor goalscoring form, and he could not find the net again in the narrow victory at Elche.
Mourinho said he is waiting for the Vinicius that “kills” games and led Madrid to two Champions League triumphs to return, and tomorrow would be the perfect occasion.
“The goals will come back, I can’t miss so many (chances),” wrote Vinicius on Instagram after the Elche game, in which he spurned three good opportunities.
The forward has one goal this season, in contrast to Mbappe, who boasts eight across all competitions.

Mourinho hailed the lethal French striker as “not normal” and the red-hot Mbappe will see the derby clash as another opportunity to pick up votes in his Ballon d’Or campaign, as well as keeping the pressure on Barcelona.
Since Mbappe arrived in Madrid in 2024, the Spanish giants have failed to win a major trophy.
To stop Flick’s free-scoring Barca, who have won La Liga two years running, Madrid cannot afford to drop many points, let alone against Simeone’s side.
The coaches clashed four times during Mourinho’s first spell in charge, three of which he won, but Simeone’s one victory came in the 2013 Copa del Rey final.
If Madrid take the lead at the Metropolitano tomorrow Mourinho will hope his side can heed his warnings not to let Atletico back in. — AFP
cf71d1141669322a: KAJANG: Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) telah merakam keterangan bekas pengerusi Felda, Isa Samad di Penjara Sungai Buloh pada 17 Sept lalu bagi membantu siasatan kes Op Fella.

Ketua Pesuruhjaya SPRM, Abd Halim Aman, berkata rakaman keterangan itu berkaitan isu pembelian dan pelaburan aset oleh Felda serta Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) yang disyaki terdapat unsur rasuah dan penyelewengan.
"Siasatan masih berjalan dan rakaman keterangan dibuat pada 17 Sept di Penjara Sungai Buloh dan dijangka bersambung minggu depan," katanya pada sidang media di sini.
Beliau berkata, siasatan itu meliputi tempoh 10 tahun dari 2010 hingga 2020, dengan enam kertas siasatan baharu dibuka, manakala satu lagi kertas siasatan lama diteruskan.

"Setakat 18 Sept, 34 saksi telah dipanggil dan keterangan mereka dirakamkan berkaitan kes-kes yang disiasat oleh pihak SPRM, iaitu tujuh kes, dan antara saksi itu ialah bekas ahli lembaga pengarah Felda dan bekas ahli lembaga pengarah FIC."
Daripada tujuh kes itu, jelasnya, SPRM kini menumpukan isu membabitkan dakwaan penyelewengan dalam Projek Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC).

"Bagi kes itu, SPRM telah menahan dua individu, iaitu bekas pengarah besar Felda dan juga bekas ketua pegawai eksekutif FIC. Mereka telah direman beberapa hari oleh mahkamah dan kini dibebaskan dengan jaminan SPRM."
Menurutnya, keterangan 30 saksi, termasuk ahli lembaga pengarah dan pihak pengurusan Felda telah dirakam berhubung siasatan KLVC yang kini selesai.

"Ingin dimaklumkan SPRM akan memperakukan pertuduhan terhadap kedua-dua individu yang dinyatakan tadi berdasarkan kertas siasatan tersebut. Pihak kami akan mendapatkan izin daripada Jabatan Peguam Negara bagi meneruskan dari segi pendakwaan dan sebagainya."
cb1449fe57c810a4: LUXEMBOURG: Flight operations were briefly suspended at Luxembourg Airport overnight into Saturday after drones were detected flying nearby without authorisation.

"Flight operations at Luxembourg Airport... have resumed following the temporary suspension... due to the detection of unauthorised unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) in the vicinity of and subsequently over the aerodrome," the airport said in a statement on its website.
The suspension was "a precautionary measure to ensure the safety of passengers, airline crews, airport personnel and aircraft", it added.
The statement does not specify the origin of the devices that were spotted. The airport says it continues to monitor the situation and warns of possible delays and disruptions to air traffic.
316d1ed7b5b3cb9c: WASHINGTON, Sept 19 — US President Donald Trump signed a bill yesterday authorising new sanctions designed to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine, shortly after it received congressional approval this week.
The legislation takes aim at Russia’s energy and defence sectors, alongside President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials.

It also targets Moscow’s so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to evade Western sanctions, and allows Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas.
This could potentially cover China and India, and furthers efforts to cut off revenue financing Moscow’s war.
The Republican-led House of Representatives passed the package by a 262-159 vote on Wednesday.
The bill would also target companies and foreign actors supporting Russia’s military, and extend sanctions involving Iran.
But the broad powers to impose tariffs sparked an unusual split among Democrats, who largely support Ukraine but have resisted handing Trump wider authority over trade.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky earlier said the legislation’s passage was symbolic and thanked US lawmakers.
India said on Thursday it would continue buying oil “through diversified sourcing.”
Trump’s signing of the bill also comes a week before he is due to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington. — AFP
994199ee9edf8144: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Two vehicles bearing the Prison Department logo were seen entering the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak at Jalan Langgak Duta here this morning.
The vehicles arrived at the premises from about 9.45am.

Plainclothes personnel are seen near the perimeter of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence at Jalan Langgak Duta in Kuala Lumpur on September 19, 2026. The purpose of the visit was not immediately confirmed. — Picture by Milda Hassandarvish

79c634cb3ac9b552: KUALA TERENGGANU: A construction contractor lost nearly RM150,000 after falling victim to a bogus cryptocurrency investment scheme.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the 59-year-old man lodged a police report at 6.19pm yesterday.
He said the victim joined the cryptocurrency investment scheme in early August after being introduced to it by an individual on TikTok who claimed to be from South Korea.
He said the syndicate persuaded the victim to invest after promising lucrative returns.
"The victim was instructed to make 14 payment transactions to 11 different accounts, totalling RM144,781.
"The victim used his business savings and admitted to having knowledge of scam-related crimes through social media, particularly Facebook.
"However, the victim realised he had been duped after failing to receive the promised returns before lodging a police report," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
d387c01e025811c7: NEW YORK: On Holding made a splashy entry into football on Friday by signing French star Kylian Mbappe, a move that raised the Swiss running shoe brand's profile as it pushes into the sport.
But On faces difficulties in its bid to translate the high-profile partnership into a sales boost in the competitive soccer market.
The brand, which is battling slowing growth in its key Americas market, is now tasked with doing what rivals have failed to accomplish: chip away at Nike, Adidas and Puma's football dominance.
Mbappe previously partnered with Nike for roughly two decades.

On, known for its distinctive "hollow pod" soles, missed estimates last month for second-quarter net sales, alarming investors about slowing growth even as it continues to take market share from Nike and Adidas. Its shares have tumbled about 40 per cent this year.
Still, the company's price-to-earnings ratio of 18.7 values it slightly above sportswear rivals, according to LSEG data, underscoring high investor expectations for future growth.
Data from M Science shows On gained market share in the three months through August, while Nike's share losses persisted.
Having expanded into tennis in partnership with star player Roger Federer, On is now looking for its next growth engine.

Its push into football comes against a backdrop of an increasingly competitive sportswear industry, from both a product and marketing standpoint, said Mari Shor, senior equities analyst at Columbia Threadneedle.
And soccer is a tough market to crack.

"Football is one of the most expensive categories to enter and performance credibility cannot simply be bought," said Jefferies equity analyst Randy Konik, adding that the Mbappe partnership signals that On needs to "spend harder to sustain growth."
Adidas sponsored 14 national teams at this summer's FIFA World Cup, while Nike and Puma outfitted 12 and 11 teams respectively.
In a statement, On cited its LightSpray robotic manufacturing technology, currently used for its running shoes, as an asset as it moves into soccer boots.

On declined to disclose the financial terms of its deal with Mbappe. But it said the structure includes both cash and equity components. Federer acquired a roughly 2.5% equity stake in On, according to Forbes, when he left Nike to join the company in 2019.
SUCCESS STILL UNCERTAIN

US shares of On, which also brought in former France star Thierry Henry as director of its soccer business, dipped 0.3 per cent in choppy trading on Friday, a sign that investors are not sold on its high-profile soccer foray.
The brand has endured a decline in the Americas, which accounts for more than half its revenue, as shoppers grapple with inflation and an uncertain economic backdrop.
Despite the publicity that Mbappe brings, "the question is whether the deal is worth the cost, which is undoubtedly high," said Morningstar analyst David Swartz.

Analysts noted Under Armour's partnership with basketball star Stephen Curry, which helped establish the company in the sport but failed to achieve the cultural influence or commercial scale of Nike's Jordan Brand. The two agreed to separate in 2025. In Europe, Under Armour has also tried to gain a foothold in soccer, but the brand has struggled to compete with Nike, Adidas and Puma.
"We view this as a repeat of Under Armour's partnership with Curry: a reminder that an elite athlete alone does not guarantee success in a category," Konik said.
Still, bringing on Mbappe boosts On's credibility in soccer, said Bruce Winder, an independent retail consultant.
The move could spell further trouble for Nike, whose turnaround efforts appear to have stalled, he added. - Reuters

603a5bc304f71d13: WASHINGTON, Sept 19 — Some companies are talking less about their climate commitments, while others are shifting the goalposts or quietly letting targets lapse.

In President Donald Trump’s second term, major American businesses are bending with the political winds and stepping back from environmental commitments in line with what scientists say is required to prevent the worst consequences of human-caused global warming.
Climate Week NYC, which begins tomorrow, is an annual jamboree of civil society, governments and companies on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

“It’s probably the biggest year I’ve had companies saying, ‘Well, we haven’t got anything to announce, so you know, I’m not sure we’ll be on stage,’” Helen Clarkson, CEO of the Climate Group, which organises the event, told AFP.

“We’re seeing ‘green hushing’ is definitely increasing, and that’s a real challenge because I think if we all give in to this idea that the word climate should never be spoken, that is a lost battle.”
The explosion of AI data centres looms large over the trend, as US tech companies rush to finance private gas plants to power them.

Earlier this year, Meta left the Climate Group’s RE100 — a voluntary pledge by leading companies to source all their electricity from renewables — fuelling speculation that other tech giants could follow.
It’s not just Big Tech, though.
Dylan Tanner, executive director of InfluenceMap, a think tank that tracks corporate climate policy and lobbying, said automakers were among the worst offenders.
“Many car manufacturers with sales in the US have weakened their EV production targets in recent years, no longer putting their push to electrify within clearly defined timeframes,” he said.
In January 2021, for example, GM set a target of 100 per cent zero-emission vehicle sales by 2035.
While it technically maintains this target, the company this year backed the Trump administration’s weakening of a fuel economy rule to a level that would require no further improvement.

“GM believes that the EV transition must account for market and consumer realities... Ultimately the market will determine how quickly the EV transition occurs,” the company wrote in a comment supportive of the rule.
First wave, then backlash

Tanner, who has tracked this topic since 2015, said few companies supported climate policy action at first, but momentum grew after the 2015 Paris Agreement and landmark legislation in Europe and in the US under former president Joe Biden.
A backlash to that first wave of high-ambition commitments began around 2023, with Trump bringing “a tailwind for some of the negative actors,” he said.
Pushback came from the fossil fuel sector and companies reliant on it, such as utilities, but also the US Chamber of Commerce, Tanner said.
Just this week, the chamber praised the Trump administration’s rule to remove curbs on greenhouse gas emissions from power plants.

In 2020 retail giant Walmart committed to cutting emissions by around a third by 2025 and two-thirds by 2030 from a 2015 baseline. But in a 2024 report it acknowledged it would miss the first target as well as its recycling goals.

Also in 2020, Google pledged to run on carbon-free energy by 2030, in what CEO Sundar Pichai heralded as a “moonshot.” But by 2024 it had stopped claiming its operations were carbon neutral, and this year it acknowledged its emissions were still rising.
Beverage giants Coca-Cola and Pepsi have changed the baseline years for their emissions reduction targets and weakened their ambitions.
Even companies whose climate policies have held steady — as with Apple under InfluenceMap’s scoring — have drastically reduced their public engagement.
Rachel Cleetus of the Union of Concerned Scientists said there was a clear limit to corporate climate action.
“I think it’s pretty clear that voluntary commitments and announcements are always going to be insufficient and we actually do need mandatory public policies on the books,” she told AFP.
“Without those policies... we just get this whiplash effect where companies are just swinging in the wind as politics change.” — AFP

f7c84e44f9eaf3db: Two distinguished men associated with the New Economic Policy (NEP) have publicly warned that its prolonged implementation has produced dependency and mediocrity.

At a forum on Sept 8 commemorating second prime minister Abdul Razak Hussein, Nazir Razak—son of the policy’s creator—described the NEP as having fostered a “tongkat culture” of dependency among Malays.
FMT quoted the CIMB Group chairman as saying the NEP was only meant to continue for 20 years, and that former deputy prime minister Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman had even labelled it a 20-year “handicap”.
“We will be in serious trouble if we have to continue. And when it goes on for too long, this ‘tongkat culture’ becomes deeply embedded,” Nazir warned.

Noting that the NEP had focussed excessively on ownership distribution and contracts rather than education and skills, Nazir criticised the absence of genuine competition, saying politicians’ discretion in awarding Bumiputera contracts and the subsequent lack of competition had “weakened businesses” and produced rent-seeking behaviour.

Former deputy prime minister Musa Hitam, who served under Razak, echoed the assessment. He stated that the policy “inadvertently produced a culture of reliance on government assistance” and had made Malays overly “pampered by the government”.

While acknowledging its benefits, Musa observed that recipients developed a sense of insecurity: “People fear receiving nothing, but even when they receive assistance, they say it is not enough and ask for more.”
Musa knows what he is talking about as he was involved in the NEP’s early years of formulation and implementation, and he is one politician who is not afraid to say it as it is.
These critiques highlight a complex legacy, as the NEP undoubtedly achieved notable milestones during its early decades but also caused considerable problems.

Instituted in 1971 in the wake of the tragic May 13 racial clashes, the NEP set out with an egalitarian dual-pronged objective: to eradicate absolute poverty regardless of race and to restructure society to eliminate the identification of race with economic function. It was also intended to unite the people.

Through aggressive state-backed interventions—including massive investments in rural education, the establishment of residential schools, preferential university access, and targeted equity transfers—the policy registered undeniable successes.

It successfully lifted hundreds of thousands of Malays out of poverty and catalysed the emergence of a broad, educated Bumiputera middle class. Professionals, civil servants, and corporate managers from the Malay community filled ranks that were previously inaccessible.

However, the policy also offers a classic case study in the unintended consequences of extended social engineering. By insulating a favoured group from market competition through quotas, political discretion, and automatic entitlements, the state increasingly substituted patronage for internal capability development.
As economist Thomas Sowell has documented in comparative studies of preferential policies worldwide, group entitlements rarely help the most vulnerable members of the target group.
Instead, the substantial benefits disproportionately accrue to those already positioned to exploit them—the political elites, the well-connected, and the upper tiers of the beneficiary group.
It rewards connections over competence and turns people into quota-watchers rather than wealth-creators.
Meanwhile, the costs are diffused across the entire population, manifesting as a sluggish economy, brain drain, diluted meritocracy, and an entrenched culture of rent-seeking.

Thinking Malaysians have noticed the persistent middle-income trap, widening disparities within the Malay community, systemic governance failures where ethnic patronage often enables corruption, and a staggering national debt burden.

It has been reported that the gap between rich Malays and poor Malays is far wider than the gap between the average Malay and the average Chinese or Indian. Rural Bumiputera, Orang Asli, and the bottom 40% in the Malay heartlands are still struggling while a small group of well-connected elites – mostly urban and politically linked – have cornered the benefits.
Cronyism and rent-seeking became the name of the game.
Decades later, Bumiputera companies still contribute only a modest share to the GDP, underscoring that the policy built dependency rather than broad-based capability.
Bright non-Malays emigrate because they perceive a rigid ceiling on their ambitions, while talented Malays sometimes harbour doubts about their own achievements under the shadow of quotas.

As Sowell noted, when competence is subordinated to identity, incentives are distorted: rigorous performance becomes optional for the preferred group, while excellence for others can be rendered futile by administrative decree.

Yet the policy persists because politicians across the political spectrum find immense electoral utility in perpetuating a loop of dependency that keeps voters beholden to state largesse. This systemic patronage has leaked into massive governance failures—such as the 1MDB, Tabung Haji, and Felda scandals—where public accountability is hollowed out behind a wall of ethnic protectionism.
When Musa and Nazir voiced their recent warning, I had expected it to spark a robust public debate on the NEP's legacy and how to overcome its shortcomings. It didn’t happen.
As the issue profoundly affects the Malays, I had expected it to be hotly contested at the Sept 9 to 12 Umno general assembly. Instead, there was silence.
No one from the government has commented on it either, as far as I am aware.
Everyone, including the media, is treating the warning as another ho-hum event.
A pity really, for Musa and Nazir are no ordinary men and their warning deserves to be acted upon.

If Malaysia is to realise its true economic potential, it must eventually confront an unpalatable economic reality: a dynamic, globally competitive nation cannot be built on a foundation of artificial crutches.

And that progress does not stem from dividing a fixed economic pie based on ancestry, but from expanding it through universal rules, unimpeded competition, and rewards anchored in performance rather than pedigree.

By grounding policies on performance-based evidence, insulating them from populist bargaining, and focusing on measurable national outcomes, Malaysia can move beyond the structural traps identified by Nazir and Musa towards genuine, inclusive progress.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

312d267d182c1ce1: PAS Youth’s annual muktamar opened two weeks ago with a multicultural drum performance – a rare sight at the Islamic party’s annual assembly. The performance combined traditional drums from Malay, Chinese, Indian and Thai cultures.

This was very different from previous assemblies, particularly given PAS’s identity as a Malay-Muslim party. Obviously, Malaysians generally viewed it as another attempt at boosting PAS’s image among non-Muslim communities as the next general election approaches.

The Islamic party has often turned to symbolic gestures such as this. Here, they invited everyone to feel the rhythm of shared unity. Honestly, it was a beautiful image with hands of different colours striking the same skin of a drum, bodies swaying in sync, a moment of transcendent harmony.

On the surface, it seemed like the perfect antidote to a worsening division in the country, brought about mainly by the pronouncements of its top leaders on how non-Muslims must play a secondary role in the governance of Malaysia.
But here’s the uncomfortable truth we rarely admit. The drumbeat is not a bridge but often a band-aid. It offers a feeling of unity that ends the moment the performance stops.

The performance may have made the youth wing feel it had done something significant about racism when, in reality, the togetherness lasted only for an hour. The next day, everyone returned to the same segregated schools and unequal opportunities, with politicians once again harping on race and religion. Racial unity needs structural intervention, not a sonic spectacle.
If PAS is serious about racial unity – seemingly the party’s lowest priority – it must stop treating it as a performance and start treating it as a structural commitment.

Unity is not something you feel in your chest during a drum performance, but something you build in your community through policy, accountability and willingness to sit in discomfort, not dance in rhythm.
The question centres on whether the party’s use of multi-ethnic cultural elements in its opening ceremonies is merely cosmetic, given deeper concerns about minority rights in its policy platform.

The underlying sentiment reflected in social media by critics reveals a deep-seated distrust among minority communities for the Islamic party, rooted in historical and ongoing political wounds. Most non-Malays viewed this as scratching the surface while the wounds are already deep – a broader crisis of trust in Malaysian politics.
This distrust is not new, as it is rooted in decades of ethnically charged politics made worse by PAS leader Abdul Hadi Awang’s constant push for Malay-Muslim supremacy.

To make it worse, PAS’s so-called multiracial political friends like Barisan Nasional and Wawasan have remained silent over the near-seditious pronouncements of Hadi. Even Rafizi Ramli’s Bersama, which has openly promised to push for more equality, has chosen to remain silent as it obviously does not want to lose any Malay support before even taking off politically.
Say it in the manifesto
The real challenge for PAS or any other political party is to move beyond cosmetic gestures and come out openly with substantive policy assurances that protect the rights of all citizens.
Here, manifestos play an important role. They serve as crucial documents published by parties before general elections, setting out the policies they would deliver if elected.

They convey a party’s wider narrative and the background to its policy choices. While governments have no statutory obligation to fulfil manifesto commitments – as we have seen in all general elections – there are strong political reasons to adhere to them, as they bring credibility and demonstrate understanding of societal challenges.
So, can PAS declare in its manifesto that its ultimate aim is to make Malaysia an Islamic state when it comes to power or leads a ruling coalition at the federal level?

Will it openly declare that it will ban all forms of gambling? With its delegates calling for a PAS minister to oversee Kuala Lumpur if it comes to power, will the party also declare that it will give the capital’s landscape a more Islamic outlook? Or like what its supreme leader Hadi has been constantly preaching, will non-Malay ministers be barred from heading key policymaking portfolios? And how will it tackle the problem of unlicensed places of worship if and when it comes to power?

If the party wins power after putting these down in writing in its manifesto, it can be viewed as what the majority of Malaysians want. No individual or party should protest if this happens, as the voters would be choosing with their eyes open. As they say, the people deserve the government they choose.

In modern democracies, the extent to which pre-election policy promises translate into actual policymaking is a key factor in political legitimisation. We are seeing how Pakatan Harapan is struggling after failing in this aspect.

There is no such thing as house arrest in Malaysia. Tiada peruntukan mengenainya dalam sistem perundangan negara.

Akta Penjara 1995 tidak menyatakan sebarang peruntukan khusus bagi tahanan rumah. Akta ini berfungsi menyediakan rangka kerja bagi tadbir urus penjara termasuk pemeliharaan keselamatan dan kesejahteraan tahanan serta pemulihan mereka ke pangkuan masyarakat.

That's the closest it gets to a house arrest.

Yang dikurung Najib -- anggota keluarga bebas keluar masuk. Tak begitu?
Najib orang politik dan pasti beliau mahu berpolitik lagi. Mungkinkah beliau akan merangka strategi dan mengatur perancangan untuk Umno dari rumah? Work from home?

Seperkara penting. Pengampunan bersyarat Najib yang membabitkan penahanan rumah dan denda RM50 juta hanya terpakai bagi hukuman penjara kes SRC International. Ini menurut Peguam Negara Dusuki Mokhtar dipetik Malaysiakini.

c0731e3dcc9092b6: From Liew Li Xuan
When Malaysians think about smartphones, they usually think about the brand first — Apple, Samsung or Xiaomi. Behind these brands is a network of retailers that brings their products to consumers.

Asia Mobile Retail, an authorised Xiaomi retailer in Malaysia, is one example. Like other physical retailers, it has to pay for stores, staff, stock and customer service. It also gives customers a place to see and try a phone before buying it, while providing support after the sale.
Yet these retailers face a growing challenge: how can they compete when consumers can often find the same phone at a lower price online?

A customer might walk into a store, try a phone and ask a salesperson for advice, only to find it is RM50 cheaper online. The retailer has paid for the store, staff and service, but another seller may get the sale.

This does not mean online shopping is bad. In fact, online competition has made it easier for Malaysians to compare prices and find better deals. If an online business can sell a phone at a lower price because it operates more efficiently, consumers should benefit.
But there is a difference between healthy competition and an uneven playing field.

Physical retailers have costs that online sellers may not have. At the same time, online platforms can also impose commissions, fees and contractual conditions on sellers. These costs can affect how businesses compete and what prices they can offer.
This is why the issue deserves attention from policymakers.

The Malaysia Competition Commission has already looked at concerns in Malaysia’s digital economy, including marketplace commissions, contractual terms and pricing transparency. These issues matter because the way digital platforms operate can affect smaller businesses and their ability to compete.
The answer, however, should not be to protect physical retailers from online competition.
If an online retailer can offer a better price because it is more efficient, it should be allowed to do so. Consumers should not have to pay more simply to keep a physical store in business.
But physical retailers should not be placed at a disadvantage either.

A retailer that invests in a showroom, employs sales staff and provides after-sales service is offering consumers something beyond the product itself. Policymakers should therefore ensure that businesses competing through different channels are not put at a disadvantage by restrictive contracts, unclear fees or unequal access to products.
The same principle should apply to government efforts to make smartphones more affordable.

For many Malaysians, smartphones are no longer a luxury. They are needed for education, work, online banking and access to public services. Government support can therefore play an important role in helping lower-income Malaysians get connected.
But support should be consumer-led and brand-neutral.

If the government provides a smartphone subsidy, consumers should be able to choose the brand and retailer that best suits their needs. The policy should help people buy a phone, not quietly decide which company gets the sale.
This is important because the smartphone market is no longer simply about shops competing with shops.

A customer might discover a phone on social media, compare prices on an e-commerce platform, visit a physical store to try it and then buy it somewhere else. Online and physical retail are now part of the same market.

For retailers such as Asia Mobile Retail, the challenge is therefore not simply to compete with other shops. They are competing across an entire system of manufacturers, telcos, platforms and online sellers.
Malaysia does not need to choose between physical retailers and online platforms. It needs to make sure that both can compete fairly.
That means allowing businesses to offer lower prices when they genuinely become more efficient, while addressing practices that can put competitors at a disadvantage.

Consumers should benefit when smartphones become cheaper. But price should not be the only measure of a healthy market. Consumers also benefit from having places where they can see products, receive advice and obtain support when something goes wrong.
If physical retailers disappear, consumers may eventually lose some of those choices.

The goal, therefore, should not be to protect every retailer from competition. It should be to make sure that businesses that provide value can compete fairly, whether they sell online, in stores or through both.
Cheaper smartphones are good for Malaysians.
But the best outcome is not simply a cheaper phone today. It is a market where consumers continue to benefit from competitive pricing, genuine choices and reliable service tomorrow.
Liew Li Xuan is a youth advocate and an FMT reader.

691bbe7b930194ab: The software engine underpinning GitHub Copilot and a growing number of Microsoft products is now written entirely in Rust, with AI agents doing most of the porting work. The migration cost about $120,000 in AI token usage plus about three weeks of a developer's time. However, managers also had to grapple with a few dozen regressions in the resulting code, pointing to AI’s ongoing challenges in understanding Rust. The effort updated the runtime module-by-module until the job was completed, spanning over 135 releases across a 14.5-week time period. Roughly 1.3 port pull requests were opened per day. Overall, agents converted 430,000 lines of TypeScript into 800,000 lines of production Rust. To keep the port as simple as possible, the port only replaced TypeScript modules on a case-by-case basis. It didn’t look to optimize the structure of the runtime itself. That work is next. And Rust, known for its lean performance, did not disappoint. One benchmark measured how quickly the runtime could complete 1,000 one-turn session lifecycles, using a shared client and 100 concurrent pipelines. The original TypeScript implementation completed 7.55 of those lifecycles per second, while Rust running in-process managed 120 per second - representing a 15.9x speedup on that particular workload. In terms of memory, a 10-client batch of agents consumed 1,383 MB with TypeScript while the Rust rewrite consumed only 126 MB serving the same swarm. Within Rust, the work remained in-process instead of spawning external background processes for completion, a requirement for TypeScript. Copilot from VS Code to Microsoft Office At first glance, most users may not know how pervasive the Copilot runtime is. It backs the GitHub Copilot command-line interface (CLI), the Copilot app, the SDK and the GitHub Copilot cloud agent. It shows up in VS Code, Visual Studio, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and innumerable other Microsoft cloud services. Originally, the runtime was written in TypeScript and used Node.js as the framework and V8 for the execution engine. TypeScript and Node were ace for rapid development, but when used at scale, they suffered in terms of providing fast start-up and server density. “This is in no way a claim that every large TypeScript program should become Rust. Our requirements emphasized embedding through a C ABI, low startup and steady-state overhead, and predictable resource use. Rust made those goals possible,” wrote Microsoft Distinguished Engineer Stephen Toub in a post that explained the entire process. The project used Copilot to rewrite Copilot, which in turn used several LLMs – GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 4.8 were both namechecked – to execute different parts of the job, depending on each LLM’s natural strength. Well-read but chatty agents Toub assessed the use of agents as largely successful. Indeed, this project would have taken years and cost millions if done by hand. Agents showed several surprising emergent behaviors, Toub noted. For one, they spent far more time gathering information than actually writing code. “The popular image of AI spewing code is almost backwards; at this scale, the work looked much more like iterative investigation, inspecting the current state, forming a hypothesis, making a targeted change, rinsing and repeating,” he wrote. Another surprise was how frequently sessions interacted with other sessions, either those they spawned or other ones entirely. One of the thorniest conversions was the session.ts file, which was over 30,000 lines of TypeScript that touched all aspects of the runtime. The porting session, which ended up taking 25 hours to complete, began by spending 56 minutes reading the documentation and making 122 tool calls for clarification. It then spawned 15 child sessions, each creating its own worktree and agent. Then, they started communicating with each other. Using a built-in orchestration skill, one session found every other active session and sent messages to those whose missions overlapped, requesting coordination. The compiler is a teacher, not an oracle Given its performance benefits, Rust has proven to be a popular language for rewriting applications. Bun creator Jarred Sumner, for instance, recently ported the Anthropic-owned JavaScript runtime and toolkit, which contained roughly 535,000 lines of Zig code, over to Rust, almost entirely using Claude agents. As of July 30, the experimental Rust port was passing 99.8 percent of Bun's existing tests on Linux x64 glibc, with the stable releases still shipping from the Zig codebase. That job cost $165,000 in tokens. But there are hidden dangers in using Rust as well, as Toub has found. For an LLM and a lazy programmer alike, if the code compiles, then it is valid Rust. But throughout the process, the project encountered dozens of regressions within the code. A regression is something that used to work, but no longer does after an update. The compiler has no idea, for instance, whether functions are in the right order, whether the job completes at an acceptable cost, whether it meets the developer's unwritten requirements, or whether it is internally coherent at all, for that matter. At RustConf, held in Montréal last week, consultant Lisa Crossman warned about the practice of treating the compiler as an “oracle,” or the last word on whether some Rust code is valid or not. “Rust stops the agent writing memory unsafe code; it does not stop the agent writing the wrong program correctly,” she said. If they’re wise, a human developer treats the compiler as a teacher, decoding the errors as a path to a better understanding of the language’s domain. An LLM, on the other hand, just uses the compiler as a black box, one it can batter with blunt, inefficient workarounds until one passes muster (perhaps this is what Zig creator Andrew Kelley meant when he called Bun’s Rust code “unreviewed slop”). In Toub’s case, he had found that compiler-approved regressions could come from ambiguous semantics and behaviors, branch drift, missing features that weren’t ported over, and differing behaviors from the replacement code. “That’s in no way an argument against Rust’s compiler,” Toub wrote. “But ‘if it compiles, it’s correct’ is useful only as a joke.” ®

87b16e708c07be91: Thanks to AI, computer science majors are finding themselves in a tougher spot than they might have expected. Jobs are harder to come by, and more graduates are ending up in lower-paying sectors like retail and food service. That’s according to a new working paper by three US Census Bureau economists examining how college graduates from majors with the highest exposure to AI have fared since ChatGPT came onto the scene in late 2022 and helped kick off the generative AI boom. The results don’t look good for those in the most exposed fields, with career and earnings prospects for the top decile (i.e., the top ten percent of majors most exposed to AI) looking as bad as those of older Millennials who graduated during the Great Recession. “The most AI-exposed decile of college majors saw their likelihood of initial employment decline by five percentage points, while full-quarter initial earnings declined by 13 percent,” a trio of Census Bureau economists wrote in the paper. “This earnings decline is comparable in magnitude to the earnings losses associated with graduating into a large recession.” And why are those earnings declining? Well, part of the answer is where the AI-affected graduates are ending up: With job prospects worsening, more are turning to lower-wage sectors like restaurants and retail, with the researchers finding that shifts into lower-paying industries account for about half of the earnings decline. The one big difference between your usual recession and what’s happening now, the economists explain, is that the effects aren’t spread evenly across all industries. Graduates from less AI-exposed fields, including nursing and many education fields, haven’t experienced the same deterioration in early-career employment seen among those from the most exposed majors. Those having trouble are largely who you’d think: Graduates in computer science, mathematics, statistics, some engineering disciplines, networking, and (gulp) even journalists are among those in the most AI-exposed fields. The impacts that young graduates are feeling have tended to ease as they move further from graduation, but previous research on those who entered the workforce around the Great Recession suggests that years of lousy job prospects can leave graduates behind the curve on earnings. The researchers acknowledge that other factors could be at play, but the paper finds that several alternative explanations don’t fully account for the pattern. Is there an oversupply of new graduates in those fields, given how popular they are? Probably not, the paper notes, and the authors explained to us. “The most AI-exposed majors saw rapid growth in graduates in the years leading up to ChatGPT's release. After its release, the number of new graduates in these majors started to level off quickly,” the authors explained in an email to The Register. “Survey data on STEM departments also suggest that enrollments in some of the most exposed major programs have started to decline.” That said, the number of those graduates who found jobs in their field has fallen faster, they added. What about self-employment or the grad school route? Together, changes in those activities could account for as much as half of the five-percentage-point employment decline, the paper concludes. In other words, AI appears to be having an impact on the job market for young people, especially those in the most AI-exposed fields, though other factors are at play. “There are many different plausible ways in which AI may be impacting early career workers,” the research team told us. “Firms may have chosen to hire fewer new graduates for reasons that are related to AI's existence, but aren't related to firms' use of the technology themselves.” Those who aren’t embracing AI in their business may simply be less certain about the future, or they may be concerned that AI is making it harder to find suitable candidates, both of which can make job prospects for fresh graduates worse, the economists told us. The takeaway from the entire paper is essentially that, yes, AI is reshaping the labor market, and it’s having a disproportionate impact on young folks who went to school to do jobs that are being affected by AI, like software development and writing. “We should be concerned about the magnitude of these results,” the researchers told us, but they added that they hesitate to extrapolate this short-term trend into a long-term doomsday forecast for the future of the labor market. “Historical evidence shows that many jobs performed today did not exist decades ago, and it's not easy to predict what those jobs of the future might be or what skills they may require,” the authors told us. “We should be very cautious in speculating about how AI will impact the economy as a whole based on shorter-term effects on only a subset of workers.” Still, the evidence to date suggests new compsci graduates fielding questions from their parents about why they’re still slinging frappuccinos or waiting tables have a ready answer: It’s all AI’s fault. ®

"Claude scopes the request, delegates the work, coordinates parallel threads, reviews the outputs, and assembles the finished result," the company explains in a blog post. "You can steer progress throughout, even from your phone, and it keeps working after you step away from your computer." It's the sort of capability that might be useful if you are prompting the model to begin a large coding project and you want to get several essential components like authorization, databases, caching, and containers up and running at the same time. Essentially, a project spins up each task as its own Claude Code cloud session thread that works on its own git branch and its own copy of the relevant repo. A coordinator directs the threads; if they touch the same code, overlaps surface as merge conflicts like those in other pull requests. And each thread may get broken down into distinct tasks handled by subagents within that session. Claude Code now offers five different ways to run multiple tasks at the same time. Subagents work within a session, though each with its own context. Agent View provides a single screen interface for overseeing several independent tasks. Agent Teams allows coordinating multiple Claude Code instances that can share information and communicate. Dynamic Workflows allows subagents to be orchestrated by a script. And then there's projects, intended for work that spans multiple repositories, migrations that require more than a single session, or work that isn't code, like a frequently queried set of support tickets or documentation. Anthropic's caveat is that projects burn through tokens quickly. "Projects can run several threads at once, and each one is a full Claude Code session," the company explains. "Because of this, projects can reach usage limits faster." Select Pro and Max subscribers should have access to the Projects beta so long as they use Claude Code and don't have existing Projects set up on web or desktop. Pro and Max users without access can join a waitlist as Anthropic gradually expands the rollout. Team and Enterprise plans don't have access to the redesigned Projects beta yet. Anthropic reportedly told investors that, in its second quarter, it posted an adjusted operating profit - if you don't count expenses including stock-based compensation. Q2 revenue is said to be $11.5 billion, and if enough customers create projects that run multiple Claude Code threads at once, that figure could be higher still. ®

de08135dfb1e908c: For a long time, sleep research has treated the cerebral cortex as a passive follower reacting to signals from the deep brain. “Usually, sleep is associated with being controlled by subcortical regions,” said Geoffrey Terral, a neuroscientist at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine in New York.

The cortex is where the slow rhythms of deep sleep can be seen, but researchers assumed the signals that triggered them originated elsewhere. In a recent Nature study, Terral and Renata Batista-Brito, who runs the lab, report a population of cortical cells that challenges that assumption.

These cortical cells make up only around one percent of the cortex's inhibitory neurons, and switching them on in a mouse puts the animal to sleep. “What our work shows is that the cortex can not only see this rhythm but also initiate it by itself, and this is sufficient to promote sleep,” Terral said.
